- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry where the object being explained is a *training path* rather than a trained network, and the matched-endpoint design makes the claim hard to dodge: five runs share optimizer, data, step budget and final gate value, and the same endpoints produce 0.734 zero-gate accuracy under a smooth ramp and 0.097 under an abrupt jump, with post-hoc continuation from the unforced checkpoint reaching only 0.178 despite a larger prior-free step budget.** Read against run 834 (the same concept re-extracted under a neutral format change producing near-orthogonal vectors) and run 833 (a recovered direction whose ceiling is set by the carrier Fisher matrix and is correctable only by the right inverse), the recurrence is that **the folder now has three settings in which the *process* that produced a structure, not the structure's final form, determines what the structure can do - format of extraction, curvature of the fitting landscape, and here smoothness of the schedule - and in each case the fix is to change the process rather than to add data.**
- **Pattern:** **The mechanism trace is the folder's cleanest demonstration of a stable *timing* attached to an unstable *identity*: across three seeds the head carrying successor-value mass is L1H0, L1H3 and L1H1, and the ablation-critical head is L0H2, L0H0 and L0H3, while the step at which ablation importance first crosses 0.03 is 1,200 in all three seeds and the step at which successor mass first crosses 0.25 is 1,500 in all three - both *after* the fade ends near step 1,050.** Read against run 824 (top-token Jaccard about 0.08 across five seeds with anchor margins holding in every cell) and run 831 (a cross-seed rotation that is Haar on the orthogonal group), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps finding retraining-invariant facts at the level of schedules and statistics and never at the level of named units, and this entry adds the temporal version: the identity of a unit is seed-dependent, the moment at which it becomes causally necessary is not.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model predicts a component, it predicts the step or layer at which that component's causal role appears as a bounded quantity and reports the identity only as a per-seed list - because a model that predicts "head L0H2" is wrong two times in three on this paper's own data, and one that predicts "ablation-important at step 1,200" is right three times in three.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry where the same concept is extracted twice from the same model under a surface change that should not matter, and the two directions come out nearly orthogonal - so "the vector transfers across contexts" is revealed as portability within a prompt family rather than evidence of abstraction, and similarity matrices built from function vectors cluster by format (0.90 within-format cosine) while those built from representational-similarity-selected heads cluster by concept (0.55).** Read against run 832 (GPT-2-to-Llama SAE-space Procrustes 0.102 against an SAE-free 0.930 on the same pairs) and run 825 (an end-to-end trained predictor whose vectors were near-orthogonal to the manual contrast and still matched it behaviourally), the recurrence is that **the folder now has three independent settings in which a near-orthogonal pair of vectors is not a failure of either vector - across models, across methods, and here across input formats - and the one common repair in all three is to score behaviour under the cross-condition substitution instead of scoring the vectors.** Mechanical rule for us: **every direction our white-box model fits is re-fitted under one surface change that should be semantically neutral (question format, language, prompt template) and the report carries both the cross-condition cosine and the KL between the two post-intervention distributions - because a cosine near zero with a small KL means the equivalence class is wide and the direction is one of many, while a cosine near zero with a large KL means the direction is carrying the surface feature itself.**
- **Pattern:** **A causal role does not buy invariance and invariance does not buy a causal role, and this paper measures both halves on the same heads: the causal (patching-selected) heads are cross-format-stable in *identity* - the same two heads reappear under all six ordered format pairs on Llama-70B, with overlaps of 4, 2, 1, 3, 4 and 4 of five - while their *vectors* are format-specific, and the invariant heads steer nothing when the concept is not already in the prompt.** Read against run 830 (three refusal vectors from different objectives overlapping about 90% at the circuit level while their pairwise cosines were 0.10-0.42) and run 828 (a probe at 93% at every layer that steered at none), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps discovering that the object which explains a behaviour and the object which encodes a concept are separable, and this entry is the first to produce the dissociation within one experiment, one model, one layer band.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model names a direction as "the" representation of a concept, the report states separately whether that direction (a) is selected by causal effect, (b) is stable across a neutral surface change, and (c) can act when the concept is absent from the input - because here the three come apart cleanly, and a claim that conflates them is the claim the paper falsifies.**
- **Pattern:** **The cheapest diagnostic this folder has found for format contamination is qualitative and needs no baseline: read the top-gaining tokens. On an ambiguous antonym prompt the function vector extracted from French prompts lifts `_su`, `_dou`, `_frais`, extracted from multiple-choice it lifts `_(` and `_A`, and the concept vector lifts `_sweet`, `_fresh`, `_bland` in all three cases - and Spanish-extracted vectors bias toward French almost as strongly as French-extracted ones, so the carried signal is "a foreign-language format was used", not the language.** Read against run 830 (a steering value vector whose logit-lens read-out was coherent only after a sign flip) and run 828 (a direction whose target token sat at rank 13,440 under projection), the recurrence is that **the folder's steering entries keep scoring the target outcome and never looking at what else moved, and this is the entry where the non-target tokens are the whole finding.** Mechanical rule for us: **every steering or patching report our model ships includes the top-k gaining and losing tokens at the intervention site, not only the target metric - because a vector that hits its target while lifting a surface token has learned the surface, and the token list is one forward pass away while the ablation that would establish the same thing costs a sweep.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry to make a recovered direction the output of a linear inverse problem with a known forward operator, and the consequence is stark: at the initial student state both the hard and the soft descent directions are close to the image of the teacher vector under the carrier Fisher matrix rather than to the teacher vector itself, so a single-step recovery has a ceiling that no amount of data lifts - and a damped fractional inverse of that same matrix, with its two hyperparameters tuned against the known answer, recovers substantially more alignment on all five traits.** Read against run 831 (a cross-seed rotation that is Haar on the orthogonal group, where the frame is random) and run 824 (top-token Jaccard about 0.08 across seeds while anchor margins held in all twenty cells), the recurrence is that **the folder has now described the instability of a fitted direction two ways - a random re-basing of the coordinates, and here a systematic curvature transform of the target - and only the second is predictable in advance and correctable in one step.** Mechanical rule for us: **every direction our white-box model fits is accompanied by its carrier-Fisher alignment ceiling computed on the same fitting data (the cosine between the operator applied to the target and the target), because a ceiling near 1 makes a poor recovery a variance problem and a ceiling well below 1 makes it a bias problem the method cannot optimise away, and the two conditions call for opposite fixes.**
- **Pattern:** **The folder's cleanest case where more optimisation and more independent data are not the same resource: under hard supervision the total error is a sum of a shrinking inversion bias and a growing amplified-noise term, so the best stopping step moves 100 -> 190 -> 330 -> 560 -> 880 as independent carriers double from 500 to 8,000, and at 500 carriers the spectral error bottoms out at 100 updates and climbs to 2.756 by step 1,000 - while the soft-supervision reference, running on the identical prefixes, keeps improving monotonically.** Read against run 828 (a floor-effect decomposition that halved the headline correlation) and run 826 (a gated evaluation whose clean profile certified the gate), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps finding its most attractive training regimes to be ones where a degree of freedom was spent silently - and here the spent degree of freedom is the step count, whose optimum is a function of dataset size rather than of the method.** Mechanical rule for us: **any iterative fit our model reports names its stopping rule and its number of independent inputs together and includes one run at a different scale of the latter, because a fixed step budget that is optimal on the small set is a deliberate overshoot on the large one and a reader given only the final cosine cannot tell the two apart.**
- **Pattern:** **Resampling is not coverage: at a matched completion budget, drawing more completions from a fixed pool of 500 prompts recovers the teacher as well as adding new prompts, and the recovery is already close to exact with a few hundred carriers - so the tens-of-thousands data requirement of the field is a noise-suppression budget for an inversion depth, not an information requirement for identifying the trait.** Read against run 820 (a per-latent survival estimate that replaced a dictionary-level overlap) and run 830 (an intervention whose route, not site, carried the effect), the recurrence is that **the folder's entries keep overturning the resource story it assumed - more tokens, more seeds, more passes - and replacing it with a mechanism that says exactly which resource the number is paying for.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model needs many inputs to be accurate, the report separates the amount of information needed to identify the object from the amount needed to suppress the noise amplified while fitting it, and tests the distinction by resampling within the existing inputs - because on this evidence the two requirements differ by two orders of magnitude, and only the second one scales gracefully.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry to separate an alignment failure into its decomposition and its geometry by measuring both on the same pairs, and the separation is dramatic: the GPT-2-to-Llama pair scores 0.102 on SAE-space Procrustes cosine while the SAE-free CCA-plus-Procrustes cosine on raw activations is 0.930, and the same pattern of a raw-space ceiling well above the SAE number recurs for every cross-scale pair - so "the features do not align" and "the models do not align" are different findings, and only the second licenses a claim about representation.** Read against run 831 (a cross-seed rotation that is Haar on the orthogonal group, where the frame itself is random) and run 826 (a gated evaluation whose clean profile certified the gate rather than the intervention), the recurrence is that **the folder now has both halves of the same insight - run 831 measured the rotation between bases and found it near-random, and this paper measures what survives a best-possible rotation at fixed dimensionality and finds that raw geometry survives far better than any dictionary does.** Mechanical rule for us: **every cross-fit or cross-model alignment our white-box model reports carries an SAE-free (or decomposition-free) upper bound computed on the same pairs, because the gap between the two numbers is the diagnostic for whether our failure is in the dictionary we chose or in the model we are reading - and a bare alignment number cannot tell a reader which of the two they are looking at.**
- **Pattern:** **The folder's cleanest case yet of an evaluation whose headline and null live in the same table: win rates are taken at the best positive strength per model-concept pair across a nine-point sweep (71.0% for the cross-model method, 68.0% native, 65.7% naive), while the fixed-strength column at s=1 shows mean signed deltas of -0.004 to +0.002 - essentially zero for every method including the cross-model one - so a 71% win rate and a null average effect are the same 300 cells scored at two different points of a chosen sweep.** Read against run 830 (a faithfulness bar cleared at 85% while the same intervention's route ablation moved the effect by 64 points) and run 828 (a headline correlation of +0.86 falling to +0.52 once floor effects were removed), the recurrence is that **the folder's most persuasive intervention numbers keep being conditioned on a degree of freedom the method was allowed to spend, and the conditioning is always reported one table away from the headline.** Mechanical rule for us: **any intervention result our model reports names its strength, layer and prompt set as fixed quantities chosen before scoring, and if a best-point search is used at all the fixed-strength row ships in the same table - because the honest reading here is that the gap between cross-model and native vectors (3.0 points, p=0.14) is smaller than the gap either one gains from being allowed to pick its own operating point.**
- **Pattern:** **The paper's own retracted run is its most useful control: the first pipeline reported a 68.4% alignment pass rate and a Cohen's d of 1.21, and the appendix traces that inflation to three named causes - features pre-selected by label confidence before validation ran, undirected pair pooling that hid the small-model gap, and a forced-assignment matcher that included weak pairs under a global-coverage constraint - with the honest re-run giving 45.5% and 0.42.** Read against run 829 (an implication about monitors that the paper never measured) and run 826 (a gate that manufactured a zero-side-effect profile), the recurrence is that **the folder's entries keep finding their most quotable number to be an artefact of a *selection step upstream of the measurement*, and this is the first paper in the folder to publish the corrected number beside the original with the mechanism of the inflation spelled out.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model's pass rate, correlation or effect size is computed on a subset chosen by a criterion related to the outcome, the report includes the same statistic computed on the unselected population, because here the difference is 23 points of pass rate and a threefold Cohen's d and both numbers would have looked publishable on their own.**
- **Pattern:** **A derived pipeline that silently degrades to the identity is invisible in the aggregate, and this paper catches one: the SAE-Feature Locator was meant to find the target model's counterpart for each of the guide's top concept features, found that none of the validated pairs contained any of them, and fell back to emitting the guide's own decoder weights - producing entries numerically identical to the native baseline in all 300 model-concept cells, which were still scored as a legitimate method until someone computed the comparison.** Read against run 828 (a probe at 93% at every layer that steered at none) and run 822 (two implementations of one macro intervention diverging five-fold), the recurrence is that **the folder's composition entries keep finding the failure mode to be the *absence of a change* rather than a wrong change, and an identity map passes every aggregate metric that does not compare against what it replaced.** Mechanical rule for us: **every derived object our white-box model emits is checked for near-duplication against the simpler object it was derived from - a cosine and a norm ratio, reported - before it is scored, because a pipeline whose translation step returns its input is indistinguishable from one that works until you divide the two.**

- **Pattern:** **The folder's first entry where the intervention's *route* is localised rather than its site: freezing every attention score at every layer - the QK half of attention - costs only 8.83% average ASR change, while removing the vector's contribution through the values costs 64.00% and removing only the direct per-head term costs 47.00%, so a vector added to the residual stream produces its effect almost entirely by changing what each head writes and almost not at all by changing where heads look.** Read against run 826 (an intervention that reproduced 100% recovery when injected at the final label token and 0% across the reasoning tokens - a *when* axis) and run 829 (a radial/angular split showing the state's magnitude cannot carry a prediction change under normalisation), the recurrence is that **the folder has now separated an intervention's effect three ways - when it is applied, along which component of the state, and through which circuit route - and this is the first to make the route a measured quantity with a one-table ablation.** Mechanical rule for us: **every intervention our white-box model explains ships a route ablation alongside its dose-response - the attention-pattern half held fixed and the value-write half held fixed, scored separately, with the caveat that "ablate the OV circuit" and "ablate the injected term in the value input" are different interventions (they differ here by 17 points), because a report that says only "this direction matters" cannot distinguish a vector that re-routes attention from one that rewrites what is read at the same places.**
- **Pattern:** **This paper supplies the folder's strongest counterexample yet to the assumption that a shared mechanism implies similar vectors: three refusal vectors produced by entirely different procedures - a class mean, a next-token objective, a preference objective - overlap by roughly 90% at the circuit level and each recovers most of its faithfulness inside the others' minimum-faithful circuits, with pairwise cosines of only 0.10 to 0.42 and a random circuit at twice the minimum size staying below 10%.** Read against run 825 (vectors near-orthogonal to a manual contrast that reached the same behaviour), run 824 (seed-to-seed top-token overlap around 0.08 with stable anchor margins) and run 827 (dictionary coherence near zero while direction alignment reached 0.91), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps finding the vector to be the least invariant object in the story - its words change across seeds, its angle changes across methods, and its direction can be near-orthogonal to a hand-built one - while the *pathway* it activates stays constant, and this is the first entry to demonstrate the pathway half with an interchangeability control instead of inferring it.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our model reports that two interventions "agree", the claim is backed by running each one inside the other's recovered circuit (or the equivalent cross-substitution) and by a size-matched random-structure control, never by cosine, overlap or token-name agreement alone - and the cosine is still printed, because the combination "cosine 0.2, faithful in the other's circuit" is the informative case and no single one of those numbers carries the claim.**
- **Pattern:** **The interpretable object is not the vector but a derived one: Gemma 2 2B's NTP vector and Llama 3.2 3B's DIM vector decode to no refusal vocabulary under the logit lens, while the per-head steering value vectors - the vector normalised, pushed through one head's value-output product and re-normalised, an input-invariant image - surface harm and refusal words for the same models, with one head (L17H6) coherent only after its sign is flipped.** Read against run 824 (a direction whose top tokens were seed-specific while its anchor margin held) and run 829 (a steering vector that was a per-example difference and never checked for being a direction), the recurrence is that **the folder's read-out entries keep trying to name a residual-stream vector directly, and this entry shows the naming can fail in the original object and succeed in a linear image of it - which means "this vector is uninterpretable" is a claim about a projection, not about the mechanism.** Mechanical rule for us: **a direction our model cannot name is re-tested through each route it can take (here: every head's value-output product, with the sign convention stated) before it is reported as an unnamed feature, because the unreadable object and the readable one are related by a fixed linear map, and the readable one is usually where the concept actually lives.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry to derive, rather than assert, that a radial change to a state cannot by itself change a prediction - under RMSNorm the normalisation divides out any scaling, so a logit collapse has to come from a component that is not along the existing state - and then to use it as a falsification test: the dilution hypothesis survives on exactly one of three models (norm ratio 0.978 on Llama, against about 1.01 and 1.06 on Qwen and GLM, while all three models' correct-token logits collapse).** Read against run 828 (a layer-selection predictor whose input is the projection into the output space, not the geometry of the cloud) and run 827 (dictionary coherence and active-feature count scoring at about zero while direction alignment reached 0.91), the recurrence is that **the folder now has a fourth independent line saying that only the component pointing at the output target matters, and this one supplies the algebra for why the alternative - the state simply getting weaker - is not available to the model at all once normalisation sits before the unembedding.** Mechanical rule for us: **every prediction-change our white-box model explains is decomposed into a component along the target unembedding direction and a component orthogonal to it (equivalently, a radial and an angular term in any normalised architecture), and the two numbers ship together with the model's normalisation scheme named - because on a normalised model a "the signal got diluted" story is not merely untested, it is geometrically unavailable, and a report that offers it has published the one explanation the architecture rules out.**
- **Pattern:** **The paper's central object is called a steering vector and is never checked for being a direction: the interference vector is a per-example difference between a conflicted and a baseline hidden state, its cosine to the truth row is averaged across samples (-0.115, -0.060, -0.146), and the mean interference vector, its bootstrap spread and the between-example agreement of those differences are never computed - so a quasi-orthogonal mean cosine is equally compatible with a common lateral mechanism and with per-example differences that point nowhere in particular.** Read against run 825 (a learned predictor whose vectors were near-orthogonal to the manual contrast and still scored the same behaviourally) and run 824 (a direction whose top-ranked tokens barely overlapped across seeds while its anchor margin held), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps inheriting the word "vector" from single-instance arithmetic, and this entry is the cleanest case because the vector is a difference of two states - which has a distribution, a length and a sign structure that the paper reports only as one scalar per model.** Mechanical rule for us: **our white-box model reports a per-example difference as a distribution before it reports it as a direction - the mean vector's own norm and consistency ratio against the mean per-example norm, its cosine to the target row, and the spread across examples - because a mean cosine near zero can come from a shared lateral push or from pure scatter, and only the consistency ratio separates them.**
- **Pattern:** **The practical claim that carries the paper - that norm- and entropy-based confidence monitors cannot see compliance - is the one claim it never measures: the motivating use case is detection, the paper's own numbers show two of three models compliant at high norm and stable representation, and no ROC, AUC or threshold for any baseline monitor is reported on the same 1,500 items.** Read against run 816 (a warning rule with no pre-window rate that a degenerate flagger could also satisfy) and run 826 (a zero-side-effect result that certified the gate rather than the intervention), the recurrence is that **the folder's entries keep ending on an implication their experiments do not license, and the fix is always the same cheap column - run the incumbent instrument on the same population.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our model's contribution is a new signal "that a scalar monitor would miss", the report includes the scalar monitor's score on the identical items beside ours, because the value of a vectorial read-out is exactly the difference between the two rows and the paper that skips the row is asking the reader to take the difference on faith.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first predictor whose input is the model's own output projection rather than the geometry of an activation cloud, and it beats the two instruments built for the job: a trained tuned lens loses to the raw logit lens for layer selection (5 of 5 versus 1 of 5 on oracle match), and a logistic-regression probe that classifies above 93% at every layer from the first cannot steer at any early layer at all - so linear decodability and output alignment are separate properties of the same hidden state, and only the one measured through the unembedding predicts the intervention.** Read against run 827 (a predictor built from class covariance whose geometry statistics correlated at -0.01 and -0.33 while direction alignment reached 0.91) and run 824 (a ranked read-out that separated token identity from the distinction encoded), the recurrence is that **the folder now has three independent papers finding that what an intervention achieves tracks the projection of the direction into the output space, and not the tidiness, learnability or decodability of the state it is added to.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model claims a direction is actionable, the headline number is that direction's projection onto the logit-lens target token on a held-out prompt set, and any trained probe accuracy we report ships beside it as a differently-hard claim - because a state that classifies at 93% at every layer and steers at none of them is the exact profile a report would otherwise advertise as evidence of an encodable concept.**
- **Pattern:** **The paper hands us the floor-effect decomposition the folder has been improvising: its headline +0.86 to +0.91 across families, computed over a population where a third to a half of the concepts have near-zero accessibility and trivially near-zero steering effect, falls to +0.50 and +0.52 on the two small models once the dead concepts are removed, while the large models hold at +0.84 to +0.93 - so the same correlation is a strong predictive claim on one scale and mostly a restatement of a rank over dead concepts on another.** Read against run 820 (a per-entry survival estimate that replaced a dictionary-level overlap) and run 826 (a gated evaluation whose clean profile certified the gate), the recurrence is that **the folder's most-quoted correlations are computed over grids whose extremes are trivially correlated, and the honest number is always the one after the extremes are removed.** Mechanical rule for us: **every correlation our model reports between a pre-hoc statistic and an outcome ships with the same correlation recomputed above a stated floor on the statistic, and the floor is justified in the text - because the gap between the two numbers here (+0.86 against +0.52) is larger than most of the effects the folder writes up, and it is invisible unless both are printed.**
- **Pattern:** **The two failures the author names are the two baselines any effect-size prediction needs: a parity family whose projected steering direction puts the target token at rank 13,440 and produces almost no effect, and a gender family whose direction points correctly at the target but whose baseline probability was already about 0.4 so there was no room to move it - so a direction has to be aligned *and* the target has to be unpredicted for an intervention to register, and neither condition alone is sufficient.** Read against run 826 (a vector whose effect reproduced exactly at the decision token and nowhere earlier) and run 822 (a comparison calibrated on common output KL), the recurrence is that **the folder's intervention entries keep conflating "the direction points the right way" with "the intervention changes the output", and this paper is the first to name the second condition as a separate quantity - headroom.** Mechanical rule for us: **every steering or patching effect our model reports includes the baseline probability of its target outcome and the rank of the target under the projected direction, because a correct direction with a saturated baseline and a correct direction with a buried rank both print as a near-zero effect, and the remedy is different in each case.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry with a predictor that is cheaper than the intervention it predicts - a ratio of two numbers already computed on the training activations - and it is the cleanest demolition yet of the idea that superposition geometry is what makes a direction work: dictionary coherence correlates with steerability at -0.01 and the number of active features at -0.33, while the recovered direction's alignment to the true direction correlates at 0.91.** Read against run 825 (a learned predictor whose vectors were near-orthogonal to the manual contrast and still scored the same) and run 820 (a rotated-partner null that separated recurrence from sphere density), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps finding that *geometric structure* and *directional accuracy* are separable quantities, and the interventions that work are the ones whose direction is right, not the ones whose space is tidy.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model scores an activation cloud to decide whether an intervention will work, it reports the signal-to-noise ratio and the mean pair cosine as the primary numbers and never the manifold capacity or the intrinsic dimension as evidence of anything - because here the two global geometry statistics are either weak or, in the within-configuration test, silently measuring which regime a point came from rather than which point it is.**
- **Pattern:** **A ratio that beats both of its parts is the paper's own ablation result and the folder's best model for justifying a composite statistic: the SNR's numerator alone reaches 0.60-0.72 on four models but collapses to -0.03 and 0.12 on the two Llama models, and the denominator alone is *negatively* correlated on every model (-0.12 to -0.25 Pearson, -0.30 to -0.59 Spearman) - so the improvement is not the numerator carrying the signal, it is dividing by class spread repairing a predictor that fails outright on some models.** Read against run 821 (a per-family usage table pricing each component's cost and contribution) and run 819 (a decomposition rule that lost its most-cited ingredient in one regime), the recurrence is that **the folder's honest composites are the ones whose authors report the parts against the whole in both directions, and here the negative denominator is the finding, not a nuisance.** Mechanical rule for us: **every ratio, score or normalised statistic our model reports ships its numerator alone, its denominator alone and the ratio together, on every model, because the sign of the denominator's correlation is a property of the model family and a reader given only the composite cannot see that a predictor which works on Qwen is doing something different on Llama.**

- **Pattern:** **The folder's first entry to show that an intervention's *side-effect profile* can be manufactured by the evaluation harness rather than owned by the method: with the vector gated to the target rule family, LRS reaches 100% on the target split with literally zero side effects on the competent families, and a gated direct logit bias achieves the identical 1.0000 / 0.00 / 0.00 profile - so "clean repair" and "a bias switch that was never switched on where it would hurt" are indistinguishable from inside the gated evaluation, and only the ungated run separates them (99.6% down to 40.4%).** Read against run 825 (a predictor's near-orthogonal vectors reaching the same accuracy) and run 816 (warning coverage reported without the pre-window rate that a degenerate flagger cannot also satisfy), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps finding its most persuasive numbers to be ones a degenerate procedure can also produce, and this entry is the cleanest case because the degenerate procedure is a *scoring arrangement* - a gate - rather than a model or a statistic.** Mechanical rule for us: **whenever our white-box model is scored on cases selected by the condition it is meant to detect, the report includes the same score on the complement set with the intervention left on, because a zero-side-effect result obtained under a gate certifies the gate and not the intervention - and the gate here was described by its own authors as a diagnostic upper bound, which is exactly how our oracle-assisted numbers should be labelled.**
- **Pattern:** **The sharpest result in the paper is positional rather than geometric: injecting the vector only at the final label token reproduces the full 100% recovery, while injecting only across the preceding chain-of-thought tokens yields 0% - so the entire effect lives in the last commitment and none of it in the reasoning before it, and the authors' manual inspection finds steered models emitting the forced label immediately rather than a correct rationale with a mismatched conclusion.** Read against run 824 (five seeds, top-token Jaccard about 0.08, anchor margins held) and run 818 (two implementations of one macro intervention diverging five-fold), the recurrence is that **the folder's intervention entries keep needing a *where in the sequence* axis and keep not reporting one, while this paper shows the axis can flip a result between total success and total failure on the same vector, same layer, same strength.** Mechanical rule for us: **any intervention our model reports is scored separately at the decision position and across the preceding reasoning positions, and the two numbers ship together - because a method that works only at the commitment token is an output override dressed as a mechanism, and no aggregate accuracy over the whole sequence can tell a reader which of the two they are looking at.**
- **Pattern:** **Cross-model transfer is offered here as evidence *against* shared mechanism: a Llama vector grafted into Qwen through a least-squares map fitted on unrelated text reaches 96.6% while a random orthogonal projection reaches 6.2%, and the authors read the near-perfect transfer as both models sharing late-layer label geometry, not as a universal reasoning direction.** Read against run 815 (a mean direction anti-correlated with causal relevance where the un-averaged spectrum worked) and run 823 (a probe's concept status flipping with the source pool), the recurrence is that **the folder has now seen the same statistic - transfer, overlap, correlation - used as evidence for mechanism in one paper and against it in another, resolved only by which null it is compared to.** Mechanical rule for us: **an intervention's portability from one setting to another is never reported by our model as a validation of what it encodes; it is reported beside the null that sharing geometry would also explain, because a transferred vector with a matched-random-projection control underneath it says the vector travels and nothing about what it carries - the unmeasured cosine against the label unembeddings is exactly the check this paper names and leaves undone, and it is the one our own steering reports should not leave undone.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry to make a direction's concept status contingent by experiment rather than by argument: with correctness labels held *identical*, only the source pool's mass relationship flipped, the same logistic probe lands above the mean-logp baseline in one condition and below it in the other, in all twelve model-dataset cells - and the steering half repeats the trick causally, where one fixed label-defined vector favours the correct answer on aligned target questions and the *wrong* answer on conflict ones.** Read against run 822 (a per-method KL-calibrated intervention comparison) and run 818 (an implementation-dependent macro intervention whose realization changed the outcome five-fold), the recurrence is that **the folder's steering entries keep finding the same edit producing opposite effects, and this is the first where the flip is manufactured on purpose and made the thesis rather than a nuisance.** Mechanical rule for us: **for any direction our white-box model reports as encoding a behaviour, the report ships an alignment/conflict ablation that holds the label supervision fixed and inverts only the endogenous quantity's relationship to the label, because a direction whose concept behaviour inverts when that relationship inverts is a statistic of the model's output distribution and calling it a concept is a category error - and the ablation costs one retrain per condition, not a new dataset.**
- **Pattern:** **The wrong-only probe is the folder's cleanest demonstration that a probe can succeed with zero concept supervision: trained on pairs of *incorrect* answers ranked only by basin mass, it still recovers held-out ordering at 79.8-82.6% on ARC-C and 70.6-73.5% on SafetyBench, so what the probe learned is a within-question scoring rule over answer mass, and the correctness signal it appears to carry is inherited from how correctness correlates with mass.** Read against run 817 (a probe with a ten-candidate retrieval ceiling reported beside its held-out-object result) and run 811 (a feature-group ranking that inverted with label prevalence), the recurrence is that **the folder's probe entries keep finding the semantic label to be a confounder on top of an endogenous quantity, and this is the first where the label is removed from the supervision entirely and the read-out survives.** Mechanical rule for us: **every probe our model reports ships a label-free control trained on the same inputs ordered by an endogenous statistic alone (mass, log-probability, length), because a probe that keeps its held-out accuracy under that control is measuring the endogenous statistic, and a probe that collapses is measuring the label - and only the pair tells us which our white-box story is actually about.**
- **Pattern:** **The paper supplies a question-level scalar the folder can use as a covariate before generation: collision concentration (the probability two independent samples agree on an answer) is linearly readable from the final prompt-token state at 63.4-78.2% ordering accuracy and Spearman 0.384-0.745 across four models and three tasks, and the authors' own geometry figure shows high- and low-concentration question states separating into different density regions.** Read against run 820 (a per-entry survival probability that replaced a dictionary-level overlap) and run 816 (a pre-onset signal distinct from post-onset detection), the recurrence is that **the folder's most useful contributions are scalars defined on the *distribution* the model will produce rather than on a single sampled output, and they are readable before the behaviour happens - which is what a predictive white-box model needs as an input.** Mechanical rule for us: **our model's per-question prediction reports the sample-agreement concentration of its own baseline outputs as a stated covariate, and any accuracy claim is shown both unconditional and conditioned on a concentration tercile, because a state that predicts concentration is partly predicting how variable the target itself is, and the two are only distinguishable once the target's own noise is held fixed.**

- **Pattern:** **This entry supplies the control the folder has been asking for since its early intervention entries: compare methods at a common *measured* output shift, not at a common knob setting - every method's steering strength is calibrated on development contexts to induce 0.01/0.05/0.10 nats per token of output KL, task gains are measured from each method's own alpha=0 pathway, and the primary budget is fixed before test scores are touched, so the comparison is at one operating point rather than at one nominal alpha.** Read against run 818 (a macro intervention whose realization changed the outcome five-fold) and run 819 (a costly output test licensing a cheap screen), the recurrence is that **the folder's intervention entries keep failing at the point where "same intervention" is assumed rather than checked, and here the check is cheap, mechanical, and takes two paragraphs to describe.** Mechanical rule for us: **every intervention comparison our white-box model reports is made at a declared output-KL budget, with per-method strength fitted on data disjoint from test, and any residual difference in semantic specificity or state geometry stated beside the number - because an alpha sweep and a KL sweep answer different questions, and only the second one is a claim about efficiency.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry from the transparent-model literature, and it supplies the one thing our interpretability-of-networks entries never have: a proved monotonicity claim of exactly the right shape - adding split families to a greedy learner's candidate set cannot lower the best per-node criterion value, because every family is written as one indicator function and ranked by one score, so the hybrid's search space contains the univariate tree's - and the same authors immediately say it does not imply better accuracy, with overfitting named as the cost.** Read against run 820 (a stability screen whose aggregate hid a five-fold-smaller per-entry figure) and run 819 (a cheap proxy licensed by a persistent single counterexample), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps needing to separate "our procedure is better by construction on the quantity it optimises" from "our procedure is better in the world", and this is the cleanest statement of the gap: the construction guarantee is real, costs 2,600x training time, and the accuracy claim still rests entirely on a 25-dataset rank test.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model's search space is a superset of a baseline's under the same selection criterion, the report states the criterion-level monotonicity separately from the outcome-level result and never cites the first as evidence for the second - because a superset search is guaranteed to score at least as well *on the score it optimises*, and the paper's own cost column (390 s against 0.15 s) is what a reader needs beside it.**
- **Pattern:** **The per-family usage table is a small, honest instrument the folder should copy: it counts how often each split family is selected at nodes, at what average depth, with what impurity reduction and what information gain, and the ranking (selective splits first, classic pivots second, plain axis-parallel third) is read as evidence that the expensive family earns its cost - while the same table is the paper's own warning sign, since the most frequently chosen family is also the one with the largest parameter set, which is the overfitting risk they name a page later.** Read against run 815 (a per-unit table separating internal lift from externally validated recall) and run 820 (a component-removal ablation that priced each statistic separately), the recurrence is that **the folder's most useful ablations are the ones that report two things about a component at once - how much it is used and how much it contributes - and a usage count alone is compatible with the component being chosen for richness rather than for meaning.** Mechanical rule for us: **any component our model selects per site ships its selection frequency beside its marginal contribution and its parameter count, because a component that is chosen most often and adds most on the training criterion can still be the one whose removal generalises best, and only the paired numbers let a reader see which explanation they are being offered.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry that prices dictionary stability as a per-entry probability instead of a dictionary-level percentage, and the shape it finds is not the one the field assumes: 64% stable at k=64, 56% at k=128, and about 16% among *live* latents at k=256, so a larger, more expansive dictionary is not a richer description but a mostly seed-specific one.** Read against run 819 (a cosine-matched "same feature" validated by behaviour and collapsing to 12-70%) and run 817 (history decodable from weights but not from activations), the recurrence is that **the folder's three most recent entries all find the object that a dictionary or a probe nominally names to be re-identifiable only in a minority of cases, and every one of them solves it the same way - by measuring something else (behaviour, held-out networks, single-run statistics) and reporting the share that survives.** Mechanical rule for us: **every feature, direction or coordinate our white-box model names ships a per-object survival estimate measured on a second fit, not a dictionary-level overlap number, because the aggregate here (56% at k=128) hides a live-latent figure of the same order *and* a k=256 figure five times smaller, and any claim of the form "feature X exists in this model" is a claim about that one latent.** 
- **Pattern:** **The paper's best predictor is a geometric one, and the authors earn it by running it against the one null that matters: rotating the partner dictionary's directions by a random orthogonal matrix keeps every crowded region crowded while destroying every correspondence, and neighbor crowding falls to 0.501 - so the 0.816 it scores on the real labels is recurrence, not sphere density.** Read against run 815 (directional coherence scoring at the random band while the SVD of the same matrix worked) and run 814 (a rotated probe keeping its discrimination), the recurrence is that **the folder's geometric predictors keep being either rescued or falsified by a geometry-preserving transform, and this is the first entry where the transform is applied specifically to the *predictor's* null rather than to the read-out.** Mechanical rule for us: **any geometric statistic our model uses to predict behaviour is scored against a null that preserves the statistic's own distribution - a rotation, a permutation within a stratum, a shuffled correspondence - because a cosine predictor and a density property are the same number until the correspondence is destroyed, and the rotated-partner null at chance is the only thing in this paper that separates them.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's cleanest demonstration that an aggregate score and the thing it is supposed to certify can be made independent on purpose: permuting each response's token scores at random leaves AUROC and the calibrated threshold *exactly* intact while moving the early-warning rate from 0.24 to 0.96 and the median lead from roughly +124 tokens (after the onset) to roughly −816 (before it), so the same response ranking is compatible with almost any alarm timing.** Read against run 813 (a calibrator that moved ECE by an order of magnitude while AUROC barely moved) and run 814 (a probe whose angle moved 30 degrees while its discrimination did not), the recurrence is that **the folder has now found three separate axes on which a single headline number is blind to the property that matters - calibration, direction angle, and alarm timing - and this entry is the first where the blindness was demonstrated by a transform that provably holds one number fixed, rather than by two settings that happened to differ on one axis.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model emits a per-position or per-example score whose ordering is its headline, the report ships an order-preserving null (a permutation of scores within the unit, an argmax-only collapse) scored against the timing- or placement-sensitive metric, because an ordering that survives a shuffle unchanged has not been shown to carry any information about when or where - and here a length-only rule scored best on AUROC on two of three models while being structurally unable to warn.**
- **Pattern:** **The two coverage numbers are a matched pair and the paper is explicit that neither may be read alone: warning-window coverage rises whenever a scorer flags more everywhere, so it is reported beside pre-window coverage, and the baselines show exactly this failure mode - the long-window repetition rules cover more of the warning window than the frozen probe on every model while covering much of the response before it, with their first alarm well after the onset.** Read against run 808 (a product metric catching a refusal collapse the primary metric missed) and run 811 (a feature-group table whose ranking inverted with the label's prevalence), the recurrence is that **every scalar this folder adopts as a monitor reading keeps turning out to be movable in the wrong direction by a degenerate scorer, and the repairs are always of the same shape - a second number that the degenerate scorer cannot simultaneously satisfy.** Mechanical rule for us: **any coverage, recall or acceptance rate our model reports inside a designated region ships the same rate computed outside that region, because a scorer that flags uniformly can be made to look perfect on the region by widening its alarms, and the pair is the only thing that separates a detection from a rise in the base rate.**
- **Pattern:** **Adaptation changes the representation and still cannot create a signal that is not in the prefix: LoRA below the probe more than doubles warning coverage on every model (Apertus 0.186 to 0.523 at the same layer, Llama 0.087 to 0.488) while the early-warning rate barely moves (0.658 to 0.695, 0.594 to 0.655), and on Mistral, where the frozen probes already have no warning to give, adapting them leaves the median first alarm after the onset - while on Llama a lower-AUROC adapted probe at layer 6 warns *less* than a higher-AUROC frozen one at layer 15.** Read against run 806 (a re-weighting that changed one variable and kept everything else) and run 810 (a steerability predictor whose in-distribution winner was the out-of-distribution loser), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps treating representation quality and information availability as the same axis, and this entry separates them cleanly: making a signal more linearly readable and finding a signal are different achievements, and only the second one is bounded by what the prefix already contains.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our model improves a read-out by changing what it reads rather than what it predicts from, the report states the ceiling the read-out would have if the target were perfectly decodable from the unchanged representation, because a representation edit that raises coverage without raising the detection-of-cases rate is moving flags, not information - and the honest interpretation here is that the adapted probe has found a judgement about the trajectory (on Apertus it flags degenerate responses more than healthy ones at any of the first 2,048 positions), which is a different claim from early warning and one the paper does not separate out.**

- **Pattern:** **The Gaussian reference is the folder's cheapest example of turning an assumption into an arithmetic prediction and then beating it: under two equal round clouds a probe that lost separation only to a rotation of theta should keep a share cos(theta), which for 30 degrees is 0.87, and the distilled probes keep 0.88 to 0.98 - a 6-to-16-point excess in all four families, exploratory p = 0.035 on four numbers, sign-mixed under instruction tuning.** Read against run 812 (a concentration curve used to justify a coordinate set without a refit control) and run 809 (a closed-form minimal-strength rule offered as sensitivity with no correlation reported), the recurrence is that **the folder's best-argued quantities are the ones that come with a stated null that can be beaten or missed, and the weakest are the ones that come with only a mechanism story.** Mechanical rule for us: **every directional claim our model makes ships with a closed-form reference prediction derived from an explicit distributional assumption (here: cos theta), reported beside the measurement with the assumption named, because an excess over a stated null is evidence and a bare number is decoration - and the assumption being wrong is itself informative, which is what the mixed-sign instruction-tuning column shows.**
- **Pattern:** **The threshold result is the folder's sharpest out-of-distribution false-positive receipt: the same probe whose ranking transfers (AUC changes within -0.015..+0.053 on a prompt set from other authors) flags 29-42% of benign prompts that merely sound harmful at its own default threshold, and an XSTest threshold set for 90% recall catches only 19-34% of the independent set's toxic prompts - so the ranking survives, the cut does not, and the failure lands on exactly the population a safety filter exists to protect.** Read against run 813 (calibration damaged by transfer while discrimination held) and run 808 (a product metric catching a refusal collapse the primary metric missed), the recurrence is that **the folder's third consecutive entry locates a transfer failure in the calibration-shaped quantity rather than the ranking-shaped one, and this is the first to state the cost in the deployable currency - a false-positive rate on a named benign population.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model emits a score that anyone might threshold, the transfer report carries the flagged rate on a matched benign-but-suspicious population at the new threshold *and* the recall cost of re-thresholding, because \"the probe still works\" and \"the probe still filters\" are different claims and only the second one is about deployment.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's cleanest receipt that a judge's own confidence is not a probability, and the ablation states the split in one table: calibration leaves AUROC essentially unchanged (0.8547 to 0.8574 on Qwen2.5-7B) while cutting ECE by an order of magnitude (0.2233 to 0.0360) and Brier by a third (0.2367 to 0.1554) - so the entire contribution of the fitted calibrator is the calibration bit, and the discrimination was bought by the guideline grounding one row earlier.** Read against run 811 (a monitor whose feature groups reordered by target specificity) and run 810 (a steerability predictor whose feature importance ranked the obvious scalars last), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps finding that the number a method reports as its headline and the number that decides whether it can be deployed come from different rows, and papers that show both make the split legible while papers that report a single aggregate hide it.** Mechanical rule for us: **any confidence our white-box model emits ships the discrimination metric *and* the calibration metric *and* the same pair for the uncalibrated read-out, because separation and calibration are independent and a read-out can be excellent at ordering candidates while being useless as a threshold - which is exactly what the component row here shows, and it is the only row in the table where a component moves one number and not the other.**
- **Pattern:** **The active-verification trigger is a threshold on the *entropy of the calibrated posterior*, and the paper's own ablation shows that spending that entropy buys discrimination with no guarantee about the cases it does not flag - the trigger fires on exactly the samples that look uncertain to the calibrator, and the paper never reports what the unflagged half looks like.** Read against run 803 (a two-step self-loop gate that fires on history rather than on whether the next step helps) and run 808 (a product metric catching a collapse the primary metric missed), the recurrence is that **every gate in this folder selects on a quantity the method itself computes, so the selection is circular by construction, and the honest entries are the ones that report the cost of the selection rather than only the gain.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our model abstains or escalates on its own uncertainty, the report includes the error rate on the retained set at each threshold, not just the improvement over the full set, because a trigger that improves AUROC by dropping hard cases has to be scored on what it keeps - and here the only threshold-free number is the run-everything upper bound in grey, which is the honest floor for anyone who does not have the budget.**
- **Pattern:** **Cross-agent transfer separates the scoring from the calibration: the stronger model's verifier keeps or improves its AUROC when pointed at the weaker agent (0.9389 to 0.9200 and 0.9137 to 0.9056) but its calibration error nearly triples (ECE 0.0550 to 0.1165), and the paper reports this as "partially agent-specific" without touching it again.** Read against run 810 (features that helped in-distribution and hurt out-of-distribution) and run 812 (a coordinate set chosen once and never refit), the recurrence is that **the folder's transfer failures keep landing on the calibration-shaped quantity rather than the ranking-shaped one, which is the same lesson as the pattern above in the transfer direction.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model is fitted on one model or checkpoint and read on another, the transfer table reports discrimination and calibration as separate columns, because a read-out that transfers its ranking but not its threshold is transferable as a ranker and not as a probability - and any deployment that thresholds it has silently assumed the part that did not transfer.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry where the selected unit is a set of individual weight coordinates chosen by a probe direction, and its motivating figure is a concentration curve rather than a claim - perturbing under 0.5% of the probe-ranked coordinates reproduces over 80% of the worst-case loss increase that a matched random set does not.** Read against run 811 (a monitor whose activation score saturated while behaviour did not) and run 809 (a closed-form per-site strength offered as sensitivity with no correlation reported), the recurrence is that **the folder's selector-shaped entries keep finding that a cheap ranking of coordinates carries most of the mass, and the recurring weakness is that nobody re-runs the ranking under a different probe, seed or layer to see whether the set is a fact about the network or about the fit.** Mechanical rule for us: **any coordinate-, neuron- or feature-selection procedure our white-box model reports ships the concentration curve (fraction selected versus share of the measured quantity) *and* the overlap between two independently fitted selections, because a set that reproduces the effect is still not a white-box claim if a refit selects a different set - and here the 1% set is chosen once, from one probe on one layer, and never perturbed the way the random control was.**
- **Pattern:** **The geometry ablation is the cleanest example in the folder of varying *where* a regulariser acts with everything else fixed, and its verdict splits by distribution: none, random, uniform and selective control are indistinguishable in-distribution (MD 25.56-27.32, NV 13.03-14.41, with the selective arm actually the worst on MD) and only the selective arm separates out of distribution.** Read against run 806 (a capability column showing the winning arm at eleven times the perplexity) and run 812's own headline table (where the full method's OOD gains are 20 points, far larger than the 2.5 points the isolated geometry step buys), the recurrence is that **the folder's ablations keep being run where the effect is smallest, and the papers that report both settings end up showing that their in-distribution evidence is a null result.** Mechanical rule for us: **an ablation of a mechanism our model proposes is reported on the matched-distribution and shifted-distribution settings side by side *and* is compared against the margin the full method claims, because a mechanism that contributes 2.5 points to a 20-point headline is either carrying an interaction nobody measured or the headline is being bought elsewhere - and the in-distribution table is where that arithmetic is checkable.**
- **Pattern:** **The probe is used as a selector rather than as an explanation, and the appendix's decoded vocabulary is the receipt that it cannot be read: on Pythia the top tokens are harm-adjacent fragments, on LLaMA-3.2-3B they are profanity, and on LLaMA-3-8B and Qwen2.5-7B they are byte-garbled or unrelated strings - yet the same probe's rankings drive a 20-point OOD ASR reduction on all four.** Read against run 802 (a direction whose sign was fixed by a calibrated threshold, i.e. a probe used *and* interpreted) and run 810 (a verdict on steering predictors that the paper declines to explain), the recurrence is that **the folder's most effective components are often the ones whose internal meaning is explicitly left unread, and the papers that say so out loud are the ones whose claims survive.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model uses a probe as a selector, the report includes the probe's decoded top-k vocabulary and states plainly whether it is interpretable, because a selector that works while decoding to garbage is a correlation about the *layer*, not a concept - and a reader who is not told this will assume the coordinate ranking means something about safety that the paper never established.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry where the monitor score and the event it is meant to predict are measured as separate variables and found to disagree in rank - the most saturated internal state (Qwen Hack, mean activation 0.966) exploits at 0.019 while a weaker state (Mix50, 0.894) exploits at 0.450 - so a high reading on a safety probe is here evidence of a regime, not of an action.** Read against run 809 (a predictor of intervention success whose feature importance ranked the obvious distance scalars last) and run 810 (geometry that predicted steerability but was never correlated with behaviour), the recurrence is that **the folder's monitor-style entries keep finding that the quantity everyone would threshold is a weaker predictor than a cheaper, noisier-looking one - and this is the first to supply the mechanism in the deployment sense: the environment's affordances gate whether the state can be cashed in.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model's read-out is used to predict behaviour, it is reported beside the base rate of that behaviour under a matched, weaker-scoring condition, because a score that saturates before the behaviour does is a state descriptor and not a predictor -- and a predict-then-threshold pipeline on top of it must be evaluated on the same labels rather than inheriting the probe's accuracy.**

- **Pattern:** **The paper's ranking study is the folder's cleanest published test that a new signal is not a relabelling of a cheap one, and the numbers are weak on purpose: influence agrees with an activation-projection proxy at 0.317 on the candidate axis and 0.504 on the layer axis, and with plain gradient norm at 0.079 and 0.346 - all corrected for the split-half unreliability of both methods, which is what makes the weak agreement meaningful rather than an artefact of noisy scores.** Read against run 801 (a cheap screen validated by its rank correlation to the full grid, r = 0.73) and run 797 (a density surrogate whose usefulness was read off curves rather than off a ranking), the recurrence is that **the folder has two different and both-correct uses for a rank correlation: a high one certifies a cheap substitute, a low one certifies that a new signal carries information the cheap one lacks — and papers that report neither leave the reader unable to tell a relabelling from a discovery.** Mechanical rule for us: **every new signal our model introduces is reported with its rank agreement against the cheapest existing signal on the same candidate set, reliability-corrected, because a high correlation says \"use the cheap one\" and a low one says \"justify this one on outcomes\" - and the decision between those two sentences is the whole point of running the test.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's cleanest instance of the ablation that separates an adaptive object from its own average, and it is cheap enough that every future adaptive method we report should ship it: keep the fitted parameters fixed and replace the per-input direction with its training-set mean, which changes nothing about the probe and removes only the dependence on `x`.** Read against run 803 (a vector bank conditioned on the source cluster, re-selected per step, with no matched frozen-direction arm) and run 802 (a direction re-chosen per prompt from the model's own refusal-token distribution, compared against static baselines rather than against its own pooled preference), the recurrence is that **the folder has four consecutive entries whose whole claim is "conditioning the intervention on the input helps," and only this one reports what the identical fitted object does when the conditioning is averaged away.** The numbers are the reason to adopt it: Frozen-QP falls from 20.43 to 13.47 `True*Info` and lands within 0.12 points of the linear probe on all three MCQ metrics, while the quadratic probe's *classification* accuracy is lower than the linear probe's (0.8893 vs 0.9286), so the gain cannot be credited to a better boundary. Mechanical rule for us: **any input-conditioned intervention our white-box model proposes is reported beside a matched frozen variant that holds the parameters and replaces the direction with its mean over the fitting set, because "the adaptive object is better" and "the adaptive object's average is better" are different claims and only the frozen arm tells them apart - and a method whose frozen arm already beats the baselines has bought its gain from better fitting, not from conditioning.**
- **Pattern:** **A maximality theorem turns a cost trade-off into a classification: the probes whose gradient is exactly absorbable into a linear layer are exactly the quadratics, so "curved but free" has precisely one member and any deeper probe pays per token forever - meaning a white-box model that wants an offline-auditable, input-dependent edit is choosing from a one-element set, and the choice is worth stating before the engineering rather than after.** Read against run 804 (a curvature measure used as a post-hoc *repair* on somebody else's direction, where the second-order object was diagnostic) and run 800 (an ablation showing that steering, erasure and rank-sweeping license three different claims), the recurrence is that **this folder's sharpest entries are the ones that pin down a function class or an intervention type rather than proposing another variant - and a negative result about the class is more reusable than a positive result about one member.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model offers an intervention with a claimed cost advantage, the claim is stated as a property of a function class with the boundary made explicit (here: an affine gradient means a degree-2 score, and a diagonal restriction means a strictly weaker probe than the low-rank general form), because the boundary is what tells us which of our own ideas are free, which are permanently expensive, and which are only apparently free because the constraint that made them free was left unstated.**

The second gap is the one the Limitations section opens: the residual stream cannot be absorbed exactly because the skip path has no matrix, so every absorbed result in the paper lives at a projection or norm site, and the seven-position table shows the best site **changes with the metric** (residual_pre_attn gives the best MC1, mlp_output the best CE) without the paper asking whether the probe's own geometry would predict which site should be used. - **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry that separates the three things an attention head does - what it reads (keys/values), what it asks (query), and what it writes (output) - into three independent transplants on the same head set, and the separation is what turns a localisation into an algorithm: the output transplant is what *finds* the 122 heads, the key/value swap on the task span is what shows the heads re-read the goal on every step (94% causal shift), and the query swap at the pivot is what shows those queries carry progress (57% against a 3% random-head null).** Read against run 783 (destination and source interventions on rank-1 signals that could not say whether the moved thing was what the head asked for or what it found) and run 787 (path patching that ranked heads by an attribution score without ever swapping the QK side), the recurrence is that **this folder has been localising units and then making claims about *what travels through* them, and only a read/ask/write split can tell an edge carrying a goal from an edge carrying its syntax.** Mechanical rule for us: **every circuit edge our white-box model reports is decomposed into source-state, query-state and output arms, each transplanted alone and each reported with its own number - because a head whose output transplant redirects the model while its key/value transplant does not is a head that is *causing* the action, and one where only the key/value swap moves the model is a head that is *relaying* the context, and the two are indistinguishable from an output-side attribution score.**
- **Pattern:** **The paper's own strongest claim is falsified-in-part by its own control, and the shape of the dissociation is the transferable lesson: sufficiency is near-total (keep 122 heads' span access, blind ~93% of heads above layer 19, ability preserved) while necessity requires roughly twice as many (blinding those same 122 leaves competence intact; only the 250-head blinding bites), and the readout budget shows the same slack - 25 heads already read the goal out, more than ~100 adds little, yet interventions need the larger set.** Read against run 781 (a four-arm matched-null suite that made an ablation's claim "these units rather than equally large units in the same places") and run 774 (a granularity ablation where the unit alphabet chose the circuit), the recurrence is that **this folder has been reporting ablation effects as a function of the set size without ever publishing the size at which the effect appears, so a redundant pathway and an inert head both look like a null.** Mechanical rule for us: **any head or unit set our model calls a bottleneck ships a size sweep on both arms - the smallest set whose preservation suffices, and the smallest set whose removal is necessary - and the two numbers are reported as a pair, because a set that is sufficient at 122 and necessary at 250 is a *pathway family*, not a bottleneck, and a single ablation at either size licenses the opposite conclusion.**
- **Pattern:** **The mechanism claim is about absence of state: the paper argues a depth-bounded transformer cannot carry a goal forward for more tokens than it has layers left, then tests not "is the encoding carried" but "what is being re-read", and the contest is decided by a 2x2 transplant where the task span beats the code-progress span even though the progress span demonstrably holds traces of the same operation (traces that only surface when their values are amplified fourfold).** Read against runs 785, 789, 790 (three entries whose decode/patch pairs came apart at a fixed coordinate) and run 783's finding that identical graphs can carry different content, the recurrence is that **this folder keeps finding the same quantity in two places and deciding which is load-bearing by whichever it measured first.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model reads the same variable at two coordinates, the deciding experiment is a transplant grid over both spans with each held fixed, and the weaker signal is reported with the amplification or denoising needed to see it - because a trace that is present and suppressed and a trace that is absent produce identical readouts and opposite models of where the next action comes from.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry that measures decodability and causal use at the same unit, same depth and same token position and reports the two as crossing curves rather than as two numbers - and the crossings are in opposite directions at the two ends of the network: middle-layer object tokens flip the prediction while their probes still miss the total count, and final-layer object tokens probe above 90% while patching them does nothing.** Read against run 756 (a probe whose firing was robust and whose causal role was untested) and run 784 (a proof that a white-box signal's value is bounded by the cheapest black-box baseline), the recurrence is that **this folder has been reading probe accuracy as a proxy for computational role, and the two are only correlated in the early and last layers.** Mechanical rule for us: **every unit our white-box model ranks gets two numbers at the same coordinate - a decode score and a patch effect - and the units we publish as part of a mechanism are drawn from the high-patch/low-decode and high-patch/high-decode quadrants, never from the decode ranking alone, because the highest-probe-accuracy unit in the last layer of this model is the one patching says is inert.**

- **Pattern:** **The alignment here is not a happy accident of optimisation but a consequence of two objectives pulling on the same directions, and the paper shows the two arms separately: with the dictionary fixed, the bilinear form is provably rank-1 with whitened-feature singular vectors (uniqueness proved, not just attained); with the form fixed, the second feature pair is forced orthogonal to the first by the reconstruction-interference penalty; and in training the singular vector moves first while the feature moves after, so the two are interleaved rather than joint.** Read against run 780 (a headline statistic and its own local decomposition computed from the same adjacency, so the local result could not be evidence for the global one) and run 783 (a reuse-versus-repurposing distinction that node-level graph comparison could not see), the recurrence is that **this folder keeps scoring one object and explaining it with a second object that was never independently measured, and the fix is not a better statistic but an independently held-fixed arm.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our model decomposes a computation into two interacting parts, each part's claim is measured with the other one frozen, and the two results are reported as separate findings rather than as a joint fit - because a fit where both move together licenses "they are aligned" and nothing about which constraint caused it, and the frozen-arm pair is what turns alignment into a mechanism.**
