- **Pattern:** **The paper converts a nuisance into a free functional label, and that conversion is directly reusable: the *sign* of the interaction term sorts heads into three mechanistically distinct roles that neither estimator recovers alone.** Negative interaction with positive pure effect is backup compensation (the head's marginal contribution shrinks because a peer is doing the same job); positive interaction with near-zero pure effect is a context-specific mechanism whose whole contribution is realised only when the downstream circuit is intact; negative pure effect with positive interaction is a harmful mechanism partially opposed by its peers. The signs are consistent within functional groups, so clustering on the pair recovers the published labels without re-reading the circuit paper. Read against run 734 (eight collapse scalars used as covariates to pick a detector family) and run 737 (a coefficient swept to move collapse and behaviour together): those entries use a scalar as a *predictor*; this one uses a *signed difference* as a *classifier*, and the classifier's categories are causal roles rather than scores. Mechanical rule for us: **when a white-box statistic has two natural reference points (two directions, two baselines, two ablations), we compute the signed contrast and report it as a categorical variable with its role interpretation attached, rather than collapsing it into a magnitude - because the magnitude answers "how much" and the sign answers "what kind", and downstream analysis almost always needs the second.**

Read against run 739 (a threshold grid was the only thing that showed a claimed timing lead survives its own free parameters) and run 737 (a coefficient swept to locate an interior optimum its own prose denied): the recurrence is that **a free parameter in the experimental design silently determines the sign of the result, and the paper that names it is the exception.** Mechanical rule for us: **any conclusion of the form "component X is responsible for behaviour Y" is printed alongside the corruption scheme, the prompt distance and the ablation baseline that produced it, and where more than one of those was varied we report the conclusion per setting - because the same component ranks first under one corruption scheme and one hundred and forty-second under another, and neither number is wrong.**

Mechanical rule for us: **when we claim a white-box statistic tracks behaviour, we report it alongside a matched statistic computed on the *other* half of the model's decomposition (features vs readout), both plotted against the same controlled knob, because a statistic that saturates at a tenth of the knob's range while the behaviour does not is a statistic about the representation, and calling it a predictor of the behaviour is the mistake this paper avoids by printing both curves.** Cross-reference run 736 (a training term that manufactures the geometry) and run 735 (head geometry generated by class support).

Against run 737 (a mechanism ablation where every row moved something, in opposite directions) and run 736 (a term whose only stake was the sign of the effect), the difference is the kind of ablation: those perturbed the *objective*, this one perturbs an *artefact* of the training schedule and shows the artefact was not load-bearing. - **Pattern:** **The folder now has the answer to the open-set half of the collapse question, and it is a warning rather than a tool: a classifier vector with zero training samples behind it is not idle, it converges to a specific direction with the same confidence and the same tiny variance as a trained one.** Theorems 2 and 3 say that with K₁ populated classes and K−K₁ empty ones, the empty vectors all coincide and point along minus the global feature mean, orthogonal to the trained weights; empirically they reach about 0.999-1.000 mutual similarity by epoch 50, i.e. *before* the known classes have settled. Read against run 734 (self-duality and weight equiangularity carry the OOD-detector prediction, so the head rather than the feature cloud is the object of interest) and run 733 (compaction moved the spread ratio without moving AUROC in the direction theory wanted), the distinction is now usable: those entries argued that head geometry matters; this one says head geometry is *generated* by support, and where support is zero the geometry is generated by something else entirely. Mechanical rule for us: **when we read prototypes or classifier rows out of a model and treat a low-support or zero-support direction as "unused", we first measure the gram matrix among such directions and their angle to the global feature mean - because the theory here says empty directions collapse onto one another and look as crisp as trained ones, and a crispness statistic computed without checking for that collapse cannot tell a real class from a placeholder.**
- **Pattern:** **The load-bearing variable is the loss's normalisation, and the paper's whole result is that changing it from per-sample to per-class is what converts a distorted geometry into the standard one - which makes normalisation a confound in every cross-model geometry comparison the folder has run.** Per-class averaging is algebraically inverse-frequency weighting, and at IF=100 the globally averaged objective prints class frequency straight into the similarity matrix (off-diagonals grading from about −0.3 in the head classes to about 0.1 in the tail, a span of roughly 0.4) while the class-wise version stays inside a band under 0.024. The BCE bias is the cleanest confirmation available in this literature: 4.663-4.669 measured against 4.6698 predicted on CIFAR10-LT across four imbalance factors, and 6.328-6.332 against 6.3437 on CIFAR100-LT, on two architectures - agreement that a free parameter cannot fake. Compare run 731 (a bound repaired by adding a reciprocal-density term) and run 732 (a score whose tuned k degenerated to 1): three entries now in which the difference between two configurations is a single algebraic term in the objective rather than an architectural or data choice. Mechanical rule for us: **any claim we make that two checkpoints differ in geometry, collapse, or prototype quality carries the loss normalisation of each, and where the normalisations differ we treat the geometry difference as attributable to the loss until a matched-normalisation comparison says otherwise - because per-class and per-sample averaging are the same architecture with different objectives, and no measured similarity can distinguish them afterwards.**
- **Pattern:** **The one prediction the paper reports failing is a conditioning failure rather than a refutation, and it is the folder's cleanest example of a theorem whose residual is numerical - the score you want is a direction of a vector whose norm is going to zero.** The empty-class vector should sit exactly antiparallel to the global feature mean, and at the theoretical minimum it does; but as the mean norm collapses toward zero any perturbation reorients it, so the measured cosine wanders (−0.6181 for BCE at epoch 600, and −0.2504 → −0.0492 → −0.0442 across CE stages in Table 3) while every other statistic in the same table is within noise of its constant. The paper states the cause plainly and leaves the quantity in the table rather than dropping it. Read against run 729 (a correlation computed on surviving seeds) and run 727 (a score whose invariance group was proved before its diagnostic value was claimed): the difference is that those papers' numbers were compromised by which samples survived, while this number is compromised by the arithmetic of a normalised angle near the origin. Mechanical rule for us: **a normalised direction or cosine statistic we publish is accompanied by the norm of the vector it was computed from, and where that norm falls below the scale at which the direction is stable we report the instability rather than the angle - because a ratio of two small quantities is a measurement of noise, and an error term that is a conditioning problem is fixed by changing the statistic, not by adding data.**

The coefficient signs say the same thing from the other direction: CTM is favoured when the representation is collapsed *and* self-dual (negative on both), while fDBD is favoured precisely when the weights do **not** align with the class means (positive on self-duality), i.e. the two most-recommended feature-side detectors divide on a property of the head, not of the feature cloud. Note the ViT explanation the paper offers in Appendix B.4 — pretrained residuals mean OOD inputs land inside subspaces created during pretraining, so class-conditional PCA filtering is the only intervention that helps ViTs, and global projection is the only one that helps CNNs. Read against run 733 (a compaction ablation that moved the spread ratio without moving the AUROC in the direction the theory wanted) and run 732 (a density score whose tuned optimum degenerated to a single neighbour): **the folder's geometric covariates are turning out to be properties of the readout rather than of the representation.** Mechanical rule for us: **when we attribute a reliability or interpretability effect to feature geometry we regress it against the head-geometry terms (self-duality, weight equiangularity) as well, and if those absorb the effect we say the finding is about the classifier rather than the representation — because a collapsed feature cloud with a misaligned head behaves nothing like a collapsed cloud with a self-dual one, and only one of those is a claim about the model's inner state.**

Note also that the paper's own three-group stratification is argued for on the grounds that a binary near/far split hides the mid-OOD winners (a ViT far clique of 8 CSFs collapsing into a focused KPCA-RecError mid clique and a distinct Residual/ViM far clique). - **Pattern:** **This is the first paper in the folder whose "explanation" is a per-sample predictive bound that is actually scored against a held-out behaviour - and it gets there by repairing a bound instead of replacing it, which is the cheapest move in the arc.** The textbook per-region Hoeffding bound (their Eq. 4) is finite only when a region holds training samples; in a deep net almost every test input lands in a region holding none, so the bound is literally infinite and unusable for ranking. Instead of abandoning the partition, they smooth the empirical error across neighbouring subfunctions with a Gaussian kernel in Hamming distance between activation patterns, which makes the bound finite everywhere and leaves a two-term score: weighted neighbour error plus 1/P(h_i), the reciprocal of local training density. Read against run 730 (where the negative result was repaired by measuring whether the phenomenon was expressible at all) and run 725 (a bound whose failing constant was estimated rather than argued away), the discipline is now explicit in three consecutive runs: **when a published bound is infinite, undefined or inconsistent in the regime that matters, the repair is the contribution, and the repair has to be visible in the score's algebra.** Mechanical rule for us: **every bound or score we publish is written in the form (fit term) + (uncertainty term) with the uncertainty term named as a function of local sample density, and we report its value at the specific test inputs where our evaluation set has no support - because a bound that returns infinity on five percent of the data is a bound that has silently decided those samples do not exist, and the density reciprocal is the term that keeps them in the ranking.** Cross-reference run 726 (a control curve that separated reorganisation from flattening), run 722 (an invariance number whose arithmetic, not its geometry, produced the finding).
- **Pattern:** **A metric that is the best on average and best in only two of four categories is reported here as a per-category *difference from the winner*, which is the honest table shape - and it also removes the reader's ability to see the cells where the method loses, which the appendix then quietly contains.** Table 1 gives only the deficit to the top method per architecture x dataset (-0.007 for theirs, -0.014 for entropy, -0.181 for the GP), so the headline reads as dominance; the absolute tables are in Appendix C-D, where ResNet50-CIFAR100 in-distribution AUROC is 0.827 against entropy's 0.859 and cluster distance edges theirs 0.754 to 0.750 on one OOD cell. The abstract's "up to 20% absolute" is the CIFAR100 effective-accuracy best case (70-73% -> 90-92%) standing next to a roughly 7-point CIFAR10 gain that the same sentence does not distinguish. Read against run 721 (six prose/table disagreements in one paper), run 720 (a multiplier quoted as 2,000x and 1,300x), run 722 (PC1 given as 68-83% in one section and 70-94% in another): the recurring shape is a summary statistic whose aggregation level hides the dispersion. Mechanical rule for us: **a comparison table we publish carries the absolute numbers for every method in every cell, and any "difference from the best" summary is printed beside the absolute table rather than instead of it - because a deficit average is a mean over cells, and a mean over four cells can be negative while a third of the cells are losses, which is exactly the margin that decides whether a practitioner adopts the tool.** Cross-reference run 729 (a correlation computed on the surviving seed subset), run 723 (five contributions, four unmeasured).
- **Pattern:** **The theoretical machinery generalises past its own paper: completeness of the bit space turns two exponential sums over activation patterns into O(M) and O(N^2 + M^3) with binomial shell counts, and that is the same Hamming-shell identity every walk-based geometric statistic in this arc needs to be tractable.** Because every pattern at Hamming distance b from a fixed pattern contributes the same kernel value, the normaliser does not depend on which pattern you are normalising (Eq. 35-36), and the double sum over the full bit space collapses to a look-up table indexed by the Hamming distance between two observed patterns, built by iterating shells and choosing which flips move toward versus away from the target (Eq. 40). Deep networks are saved from an intractable partition only by assuming the *full* bit space - which is precisely the idealisation that assigns density to unreachable regions and that the authors list as a limitation. Read against run 728 (LC computed by one forward pass over a sampled hull) and run 729 (folding by a walk whose bit gaps exceed one in deep layers), the shared constraint is now clear: every cheap partition statistic in this folder is bought by pretending the feasible pattern set is the whole bit cube. Mechanical rule for us: **when we adopt a cheap partition or walk statistic we state which idealisation purchased the cheapness - full bit space instead of the feasible set, last layer only, sampled hull instead of the region - and we measure the error that idealisation introduces at least once, because the exponential-to-polynomial trick here is valid exactly when the reachable set is the cube, and the paper's own numbers are then a lower bound rather than an estimate.** Cross-reference run 727 (an extension whose lost structure the authors named in the same paragraph), run 725 (bias-only noise as the perturbation that keeps the geometry).

- **Pattern:** **The headline correlation is computed on the one seed out of five where the experiment worked, and the authors print the failure rate in the same paragraph - this is the folder's cleanest case of a depth correlation that is really a survivorship correlation.** Box 1 of `arxiv-2503.08502` (run 727) quoted this paper as the empirical authority for folding rising with depth and for folding tracking generalisation, and it turns out the support is a single Pearson 0.987 on seed 4, with seeds 3 and 4 the only ones of {0,1,2,3,4} to hit target accuracy and the 6- and 10-layer nets the ones that fall to about 0.85 - so the depth sweep is correlated with depth using only the depths that trained, on the only seeds that trained them. Read against run 722 (a defect magnitude that separated two groups retrospectively, with the author saying so), run 720 (an optimiser contrast confounded by loss level), and run 713 (numbers inherited from a survey): the recurring failure mode is not a wrong number but a number whose denominator is the subset that survived. Mechanical rule for us: **every correlation we publish across an architectural or training variable ships with the seed count attempted, the seed count that reached the criterion, and the swept values of both quantities - and where the criterion is itself accuracy we state the criterion - because a correlation over surviving seeds and surviving depths is a statement about which configurations trained, and the sweep variable and the survivor filter are not independent.** Cross-reference run 721 (a stated conclusion re-derived from its own table and found reversed), run 716 (a boundary chosen against the outcome it explains).
- **Pattern:** **The paper's one genuinely exact result is a theorem that confines folding to depth two or more, and its proof doubles as the cleanest re-derivation of why one hidden layer cannot separate XOR - geometry from a theorem rather than from a dataset.** Lemma 1 asserts convexity of a union of activation regions is equivalent to Hamming convexity of the bit patterns, and the forward direction is just the observation that crossing a whole-space hyperplane flips exactly one bit, so a straight segment is a shortest Hamming path; the reverse direction says a convex bit set forces the corresponding region union to be convex. The load-bearing hypothesis is *whole-space hyperplane* - first-layer neurons only - and the authors state the cost in the same section: deeper layers produce adjacent regions whose patterns differ by more than one bit, which is precisely what Example 2 exhibits on CantorNet. Compare run 727 (an extension whose lost structure the authors named in the same paragraph: the same discipline), run 718 (a framework whose five contributions included one theorem and four claims), run 724 (an exact re-description yielding zero measured numbers - the benign version of the same shape). Mechanical rule for us: **a theorem we lean on is cited together with its hypothesis, and where that hypothesis names a layer - first layer, whole-space hyperplane, single linear piece - we check before use whether the statistic we are computing lives in a deeper layer and say so in the entry, because the equivalence that justifies a walk statistic on layer one is exactly the one that fails by layer two, and a theorem's scope is part of its statement.** Cross-reference run 725 (a result valid only for the perturbation family it was proved for - bias noise), run 723 (a rank statistic whose threshold silently decided the reading).
- **Pattern:** **The measure is bounded and the bound is offered as its fitness for comparison, which is the second paper in three runs to sell a statistic on its invariance group rather than on its diagnostic value - and here the bound is proved while the diagnostic content is a hypothesis the authors label as such.** Lemma 2 gives 0 <= chi <= 1 for any path crossing more than one region, and the Discussion turns that into the programme's pitch: boundedness makes the score a reference point usable across models. What it is *not* shown to do is predict anything - the generalisation link is written as a hypothesis under an explicit "The question / The answer" heading, and the tests that would earn it (random labels in 10% steps, adversarial perturbations, augmentation, learning-rate and optimiser variation, neuron subsets) are listed in §7 as work for others. Read against run 727 (where the same group proved invariances before promising diagnostic value, and were honest that the claim was untested) and run 726 (a control that made a claim falsifiable), the arc's discipline is now clear and reusable. Mechanical rule for us: **we separate a statistic's range and invariances from its predictive content in separate sentences, we let boundedness license comparison across models and nothing else, and we never let a normalised score stand in for a mechanism - because [0,1] is a scale, not a finding, and the denominator that produces it (total Hamming distance walked) moves whenever the walk's step count or step rule moves.** Cross-reference run 722 (a residual fraction whose invariance followed from dimension, not dynamics), run 723 (rho_exec/rho_rand, where the ratio was the finding and the invariance was noise).

- **Pattern:** **The cheapest partition statistic in this folder's reach is a hyperplane-cut count over a sampled hull, and this paper is where the random-probe control was introduced - which makes it the origin of the control that runs 723-727 each re-derived independently.** Around a probe point the authors draw P orthonormal offsets, push the hull's vertices through in one forward pass, and count per layer how many pre-activations change sign across the vertices; no labels, no loss, no task, and it reproduces the doubly-descending curve that an exact region-count method (SplineCAM) gives on the same MLP. Read against run 726 (the three-probe-set rule credited to a 2024 paper) and run 725 (bias-perturbed boundary density averaged over the data distribution), the lineage is now visible: the random-point curve is not an innovation of the later papers, it is already here, plotted as a third colour beside train and test and doing exactly the job it does later - separating "the partition reorganised near the data" from "the partition changed everywhere", since the train-side ascent does not appear at random points. Mechanical rule for us: **when we adopt a control from a paper we cite the paper that introduced it rather than the one that restated it, and any locality claim we make is accompanied by the random-point version of the same statistic computed on the same checkpoints - because the random curve is what turns "the model uses dense regions near the data" into a falsifiable statement about where the boundaries are.** Cross-reference run 726 (LC at data, shifted and random probes), run 727 (invariance group stated before a statistic is used).
- **Pattern:** **The same manipulation moves the phenomenon in opposite directions across two architectures inside this one paper, and the authors report both - so the trajectory is the finding and the direction of every effect is a per-setting fact.** Depth reduces the ascent peak and the train-test LC gap on MNIST MLPs, but under induced grokking depth raises the ascent peak and delays generalisation; on CIFAR10 CNNs depth raises the ascent peak and train-test LC are nearly indistinguishable throughout, where on MNIST the ascent is almost entirely a training-set effect. Width is non-monotone even within one setting: climbing 20 to 1000 starts the ascent earlier and higher, and 2000 lowers the peak again. Two regularisers that both "remove the final descent" do so with opposite side effects - batch norm raises LC on train, test and random points, weight decay lowers the ascent peak and shortens it. This is the honest shape of a phenomenon paper and it is citable precisely because the disagreement is printed: the three-phase shape survives every sweep while every specific direction flips at least once. Mechanical rule for us: **we distinguish, in our own write-up and in every entry we cite, a shape claim from a direction claim - a shape that survives N settings is evidence, a direction observed in one setting is a hypothesis - and where an architecture family changes the direction we report the two families side by side rather than averaging them, because a mechanism whose sign depends on the architecture is a mechanism that depends on something not yet named.** Cross-reference run 722 (three spectral objects in one paper telling three different stories), run 721 (six prose/table disagreements in one paper), run 727 (a score whose invariance group decided what it could be compared with).
- **Pattern:** **The migration story is carried by pictures plus a handful of slice counts, and the paper's own conclusion concedes there is no theory - which places the whole arc's central object on the demonstration side of the line, again.** Exact partition visualisations on 2-D slices through three training samples show boundaries crowding onto training points during the ascent and moving to the decision boundary during the second descent; the quantitative support is the LC curve and exact counts on select slices, never a boundary-distance distribution over the input distribution. The Conclusion states that the phases remain unexplained and that the work rebuts earlier stationary-partition assumptions without offering a replacement model. Compare run 724 (an exact re-description that measured nothing), run 726 (region counts on four selected slices standing in for a distribution), run 723 (four of five contributions claimed rather than measured): four papers in this arc now describe the same migration and none measures where the boundaries go as a distribution. Mechanical rule for us: **a geometric mechanism we claim is carried by a distribution-level statistic - mean distance from probe points to the nearest region boundary, or the share of sampled points whose neighbourhood has any boundary at all - measured at every checkpoint, so that "boundaries migrated" is a number that could have come out flat; slice pictures are illustration, and an entry that cites migration without such a statistic says so.** Cross-reference run 725 (boundary density made local and data-weighted - the closest existing instrument), run 724 (exactness is not diagnostic evidence).

The random-probe curve forces the claim into its real form: boundaries leave the data neighbourhoods and concentrate somewhere the random probes do not sample, which is then verified on the slice. Note the cost - 1,000 ResNet18 probes in about 28 s on an RTX 8000 - so this control is cheap enough to be mandatory rather than aspirational. Mechanical rule for us: **every locality statistic we report (boundary density, region count, curvature, rank) is reported at three probe sets - the data, a distribution-shifted set, and uniformly random points - because a statistic computed only at the data cannot distinguish "the model reorganised" from "the model flattened", and the random set is the null that separates them.** Cross-reference run 725 (bias-perturbed boundary density weighted by the data distribution), run 722 (a residual fraction whose only informative form was its ratio to a random basis), run 714 (a spread statistic whose value was set by the random-initialisation baseline).
- **Pattern:** **The paper's own diagnostic for whether its measure is valid is the most portable instrument in it, and it is a test of the neighbourhood rather than of the network: push the probe polytope through the layers and measure how much its shape deforms.** Graph eccentricity and diameter of the polytope rise roughly exponentially with depth for larger radii and stay flat below about 0.014 on CIFAR10 and for the ResNet18, which is why the radii used are 0.005 and 1e-4 rather than something more local; and even then the authors report that the LC *dynamics* are similar across large and small radii, so the qualitative curve survives the approximation even where the absolute value does not. This is the first entry in the folder that pays for a hyperparameter with a measurement instead of asserting it, and the same operation is what ordinary probing lacks: a linear probe never checks whether the representation neighbourhood it is reading still corresponds to an input neighbourhood. Mechanical rule for us: **any statistic computed on a pushed-forward neighbourhood (a polytope, a ball, a patch of activation space) ships with the deformation of that neighbourhood measured at the depth it was taken, and the radius is chosen as the largest one where deformation is still flat - because a local statistic taken through a deep network is a statement about an object that may no longer be local by the time you read it.**
- **Pattern:** **Region counting and circuit counting are the same measurement here, and the paper says the identity out loud - a region is one active-neuron configuration, adjacent regions differ by one neuron, so boundary density around a point *is* circuit-transition density around that point.** That single sentence collapses two literatures this folder has been reading separately (the spline/partition line from runs 718, 723-725 and the mechanistic circuit line), and it comes with the empirical claim that circuits are exhausted rather than accumulated late in training: the partition coarsens around data and concentrates on the boundary, so the number of distinct subgraphs traversed in a data locality collapses, most sharply in the deeper layers. The load-bearing caveat is that the paper's own theory stops before this: it offers no account of why the migration happens only after interpolation, and the association between migration and robustness is never tested by moving boundaries artificially. Mechanical rule for us: **when we write that a feature or circuit "is used", we state the measure as a density over an input locality and report how that density changes over training, and we treat a dense-region count and a circuit count as one statistic rather than two corroborations - because counting regions and counting circuits from the same partition is one measurement, and two names for one number is not evidence.**

- **Done:** arxiv-2412.18283 - On the Local Complexity of Linear Regions in Deep ReLU Networks (read full v3 HTML, 134,483 chars / 2,591 lines: abstract, §1-§2, §3 with Def. 1 / Thm. 2 / Cor. 3, §4 with Def. 4 / Thm. 5, §5 with Prop. 6 / Thm. 7, §6 with Prop. 8 / Prop. 9 / Cor. 10, §7 including the complete Limitations and future research section, the reference list in full, Appendix A.1-A.12 (notation, the single-neuron and two-hidden-layer worked computations, every proof), Appendix B.1-B.4 (estimation, sigma ablation, init-scale ablation, bound tightness), Appendix C.1-C.4; Figures 1-14 read from captions and reporting prose, **not inspected as images**; **the paper contains no tables at all**, so every number in the entry comes from prose or a figure caption)
- **Pattern:** **The paper's real contribution is a definition that makes the partition object answerable to the data distribution, and the trick that buys it is perturbing biases only - which is the missing half of every partition statistic this folder has been computing.** Counting regions at fixed weights needs a parametric solve; averaging the boundary density over Gaussian *bias* noise needs only a co-area formula, and bias noise translates boundaries without rotating them, so the averaged object is still the same geometry (their sigma ablation at 0.025/0.05/0.1 and the bias-vs-bias+weight comparison in Appendix B.1 both leave the picture qualitatively unchanged). Theorem 2 then factorises that density into a per-neuron term, ‖∇z_i(x)‖ × ρ_b(z_i(x)) × 1{z_i good at x}, i.e. gradient norm times a threshold-crossing weight times a liveness indicator. Read against run 724 (the radius dropped from the power-diagram object, so a centroid can name a tile the input does not occupy) and run 723 (a rank at a fixed 90% variance cut measuring the measurement), this is the third consecutive run arriving at the same structural point from a different direction: a geometric quantity computed in ambient space is not a statement about the network until it is weighted by where the data is. Mechanical rule for us: **every partition, region, curvature or boundary statistic we report is averaged over a data distribution (or an explicit input sample) rather than over input space, is computed under a perturbation that moves boundaries without re-orienting them (bias noise), and is reported per neuron as gradient-norm times threshold-crossing so the contribution can be attributed - because a region count in ℝ^D upper-bounds nothing about behaviour, and a boundary density near the data is the only version of the object that a mechanism could act through.**
- **Pattern:** **The one place the paper's own bound fails, it diagnoses the failure by measuring a constant inside the bound instead of softening the claim - and calls the result unexpected rather than rescued; this is the template the folder should copy for every relation it publishes.** Total variation and local complexity drop together on MNIST at 2× He initialization, which is the setting they chose; at standard He initialization the correlation "seems to break down", and at 3× the picture changes again (Appendix B.3, Figure 8). Rather than hedge, they estimate the bound's own Lipschitz term as the max over layers of the suffix matrix-product operator norm, show the corrected lower bound resumes tracking LC across 88 repeated runs (Figure 9), and then state that the late-training TV *spike* is attributable to growing Lipschitz constants and "merits further investigation" - an inconclusive diagnosis reported as inconclusive. Note against run 721 (six prose/table disagreements where the reversed ordering supported the thesis) and run 722 (an invariance number the author himself called nearly contentless): those authors reported the doubtful number; this one reported the ablation that broke it. Mechanical rule for us: **when a predicted relation fails under our own ablation, we do not drop the ablation from the write-up - we estimate the constant that could absorb the discrepancy, re-test with that estimate, and state plainly whether the estimate rescued the bound or whether the residual is unexplained; because a bound with unmeasured constants is untestable in the regime where it matters, and the only honest outcome is a named residual.**
- **Pattern:** **Local rank is defined here as `rank_ε` - a count of singular values above a threshold - and the theory's relation to local complexity runs through that ε twice, which is an independent theoretical confirmation of the folder's empirical complaint about r90.** Theorem 5 bounds LC above by Σ_l √(C²·LR^ε_l + ε²n_l) and bounds Σ_l LR^ε_l above by (LC + error terms)/(c·ε²); both directions carry the threshold explicitly, and the exact-rank corollary only survives in the limit ε→0 through a weaker √LR form. Also worth holding: the paper's own Figure 12 shows local-rank dynamics on MNIST can be considerably more complex than on the synthetic task, and their Figure 2 correlation numbers (0.852 / 0.957 / 0.985 at layers 2/3/4) come from a 100-dimensional Gaussian-to-Gaussian regression with a randomly drawn cross-covariance, i.e. from the one setting where a low-rank target is known to exist. Read against run 723 (r90 at a fixed 90% variance cut with no null and no spectrum) and run 719 (a null the same paper had already shown to be wrong by orders of magnitude), this closes the loop from the theory side. Mechanical rule for us: **when we quote a rank we state ε (or the variance cut) and the spectrum it was cut from, we report the rank at two thresholds, and we never present a rank correlation obtained on a synthetic low-rank target as evidence about the rank of a trained network's features - because rank_ε is monotone in ε by definition, and a correlation between two thresholded quantities is partly a correlation between two thresholds.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the analytical parent of run 710's empirical paper, and reading it dissolves the distinction that four earlier runs were groping for: the "spectral edge" and the optimiser's coherent direction are not the same object, they are the *subspace* and its *basis*.** Run 717 found that a parameter-space diagnostic subspace was interchangeable with random directions of the same rank; run 718 found the general geometric object (a centroid of an affine tile) that the whole programme is a probe of; this paper supplies the skeleton both were standing inside - a dominant block of k* modes separated from a subdominant block by one gap, with the entire dynamic content in the gap size. The load-bearing move is that "signal versus noise" is the wrong axis in this regime. With p/W around ten million the classical Baik–Ben Arous–Péché threshold sits orders of magnitude below the weakest mode, so every mode is signal and the interesting boundary is between committed and wandering signal. For us this is the correct frame for reading weights: our problem is not detecting directions, it is telling the directions the network has settled on from the ones it is merely passing through. Mechanical rule for us: **report any spectrum-derived statement with its aspect ratio and with the position index at which it was taken, and never quote a signal/noise separation that came from an isotropic null without also reporting the empirical spread of the noise modes in the same window** - because when the null is off by two orders of magnitude, as run 710 already measured, the null is describing a different problem.
- **Pattern:** **The paper's most portable instrument is a stability coefficient computed by splitting the window in half, and its most instructive result is that the instrument loses to its own simplest component at the window sizes a practitioner would actually use.** The coefficient is one minus the ratio of window perturbation to squared gap, floored at zero, and it needs no Hessians and no gradients - just the spectrum. It is what makes "how reliably is this direction held" a number. But the causal sweep (§28) reports rank correlation 0.21 and 0.42 at windows of 10 and 20 checkpoints against 0.76 and 0.72 for the plain gradient product, crossing over only at 30 (0.75 versus 0.63) and 40 (0.68 versus 0.35). The paper reads the crossover as the minimum window for resolving subdominant modes and that is probably right; the consequence it does not draw is that most published trajectory analyses use windows of ten to twenty. Compare run 711 (a percentile statistic stable where a maximum swung two orders of magnitude, visible only because both were tabulated) and run 718 (a surrogate graded by recovering a single known answer). Mechanical rule for us: **a correction term added to a simple score is reported with the simple score's value alongside it at every setting we actually used, and the claim "the correction helps" is only made above the crossover point where it demonstrably does - because a two-parameter refinement that wins at a window size nobody chose a priori is a refinement tuned by the sweep.**
- **Pattern:** **The control design here is a hyperparameter contrast dressed as a mechanism test, and the paper is honest enough in its phrasing that the gap shows.** The headline is 24/24 grokking runs with weight decay against 1/24 without, with the sub-leading gap compressing 33-43x at the grokking step. The author's own wording - weight decay as a driver "by which" the dynamics are associated with generalisation - concedes the association. Meanwhile the one test that does intervene, removing a signal direction from the updates and comparing against the predicted per-direction loss change (§28), is the one that came back window-limited, and the one prediction that came back null (gap-flow sign correlation r = +0.08, R² = 0.006) is excused by the equation having three terms rather than retested. - **Done:** arxiv-2604.11962 - The Linear Centroids Hypothesis: How Deep Network Features Represent Data (read full text v1: abstract, §1-§5 including Discussion, Limitations, Impact Statement and Acknowledgments; Appendices A-H including the formal theory, the polygon/GELU replications, MNIST, the Platonic-representation check and the compute table; displayed maths read from the TeX pass; Figures 1-17 read from captions and reporting prose, not inspected as images; reference list read in full)
- **Pattern:** **This is the first entry in the folder that relocates the feature from the layer's output space to its *input* space and gets a falsifiable prediction out of the move - and the prediction is a dissociation, which is worth more to us than any accuracy gain it reports.** Because a centroid is the Jacobian of a sub-component summed over output dimensions (`J^T·1`), it describes what the local affine map *does*, whereas a latent activation describes only *where the input landed*. The paper's load-bearing experiment follows directly: inject colour into FashionMNIST at a swept correlation with the label, then probe colour linearly from latents and from centroids. Latents stay linearly decodable for colour even at random correlation; centroids are decodable only to the extent the label depends on colour. That is a claimed criterion for spuriousness - present-but-unused versus used - and it is the first operational test this folder holds for the distinction every "spurious feature" warning since run 690 has gestured at. Caveat that must travel with it: the evidence is a left-hand panel of a figure with no tabulated effect size and no seed spread, so the dissociation is demonstrated in kind, not in magnitude. Mechanical rule for us: **for every feature we report, we report both readings - the representation-side one (is it linearly decodable from activations?) and the action-side one (does removing or perturbing it move the output map?) - and we call a feature spurious only when the first is positive and the second is flat, because a direction being present is not the same as a direction being used, and only a pair of readings can separate them.** Cross-reference run 717 (a diagnostic subspace interchangeable with random of the same rank - the same "presence is not use" failure, met from the causal side), run 695 (a construction baseline making a score interpretable).
- **Pattern:** **An attribution score computed as a mean relative displacement over a neighbourhood is an intervention-shaped quantity obtained without running the intervention, and this folder now has the clean statement of what such a surrogate buys and what it does not.** Ablating one neuron and measuring the relative change in the sample's centroid, then averaging over a 256-point ball of radius 0.25 around the input embedding, ranks the previously published "an"-neuron of GPT2-Large in the top 99.8th percentile of its layer at layer 31 - a filter that avoids sweeping every neuron, arrived at from one prompt. Two properties are checked (low variance across draws, stable percentile across neighbourhood sizes) and one is not: the score is never validated against the ablation it stands for. So the claim "this ranking matches what ablation would find" rests on one recovered known answer, i.e. a test on the training case. Compare run 696 (a shuffled-community null beating every activation-only score) and run 717 (a 648x coupling ratio falling monotonically to 140 as the estimator is made less trivial) - both are cases where a surrogate was graded against itself. Mechanical rule for us: **any cheap surrogate for an expensive intervention (a gradient-based attribution, a centroid displacement, a Jacobian norm) is graded by rank correlation against the expensive intervention on a held-out set of at least dozens of cases, reported as a scatter and a Spearman value, and a surrogate validated only by recovering a single known answer is described as "consistent with" rather than "predicts".** Cross-reference run 694 (the one-forward-pass screen, first column only), run 696 (the shuffled null), run 717 (the degenerate-estimator limit).

This is one level sharper than the folder's previous warnings (run 715: necessary in one seed, inert in another; run 716: one implementation among several) because here the diagnostic and the null are evaluated in a single experiment on one model. Mechanical rule for us: **every time we report that a recovered direction, feature or subspace "matters", we also report the same intervention with a random subspace of the same dimension at the same site, and if the two are statistically indistinguishable we write "rank, not direction" - because a coupling ratio, however large and however reproducible, is a property of the measurement geometry, and only the matched-random intervention tells us whether the direction is doing the work.** Cross-reference run 714 (a circuit necessary in s42 and inert in s271), run 716 (every sink component individually dispensable), run 707 (magnitude and direction separated by three ratios).
- **Pattern:** **Most of a spectral coupling number can be inherited from shared Jacobians rather than from feature structure, and the window sweep here is the folder's best instrument for detecting it.** At W=1 the rolling SVD reduces to the normalised instantaneous gradient, and the coupling ratio is 648x; the author states outright that this is near-tautological because the parameter gradient and the embedding-space centroid are built from the same Jacobians, so any perturbation along the gradient moves centroids mechanically. The ratio then falls monotonically with the window - 648 at W=1, 617 at W=2, 394 at W=5, 212 at W=20, 140 at W=40 - which makes the canonical setting a chosen averaging timescale, not a discovery. The paper is honest about this (it says the "spectral edge" contribution is not load-bearing in single-task) and it is the reason its multitask result is the real one. Mechanical rule for us: **any sensitivity or attribution number produced by perturbing a model along a quantity derived from its own gradients is reported together with the degenerate-parameter limit of that estimate (W=1, instantaneous, single-batch) and the ratio between them - because a chain-rule-implied response is not evidence of a privileged feature direction, and only the decay curve as the estimator is made less trivial tells us how much of the number survives.** Cross-reference run 716 (the Marchenko-Pastur null rejected by 229-576x yet still used as the detection floor), run 706 (variance versus magnitude separated by a norm-matched control), run 708 (a scale fixed at initialisation decides what the fit finds later).

- **Pattern:** **A trajectory statistic chosen as an argmax over candidates, and then validated by its correlation with the very target it is supposed to predict, is a fit and not a discovery - and this paper is the folder's clearest case because the winner changes with scale.** The signal/noise boundary is defined as the k maximising the ratio of consecutive singular values. At 51M that is sigma2/sigma3 (peak 1.747 ± 0.120 across four seeds) and it correlates with validation loss at |r| = 0.738. At 124M the paper ranks all five candidates by their loss correlation, and sigma2/sigma3 - the boundary that WAS the edge at 51M - comes **last** at 0.211, while sigma3/sigma4 wins at 0.870. The author then writes that "the correct spectral edge automatically emerges as the ratio most strongly coupled to training dynamics", which is selection on the outcome stated as if it were a property of the object. There is no a-priori rule for which ratio is the edge at a new scale. Mechanical rule for us: **any boundary, threshold or rank we define as the argmax of a ratio over a candidate family ships with the full candidate table, the rank of the winner against the outcome it explains, and an explicit note when that ranking chose it - and the word "emerged" is reserved for cases where the winner was fixed before the outcome was measured; otherwise we write "selected", and the selected statistic has to be cross-validated on held-out windows before it counts as predictive.** Cross-reference run 714 (spread-versus-integral ranking: the naive summary ranks the random-init collapse at the top while the integral ranks the real specialists - the same trap inside the model's own features), run 712 (a percentile threshold is stable where a maximum swings two orders of magnitude).
- **Pattern:** **When the null model is rejected by two orders of magnitude it cannot also be the detection floor in the same paper - and here the paper knows both things and reports both anyway.** Marchenko-Pastur predicts a noise-eigenvalue coefficient of variation of about 0.001 at this aspect ratio; the observed value is 0.688 at 51M and 0.26-0.50 at 124M, a factor of roughly 229-576. The author's own diagnosis is that Adam's second-moment preconditioner structures the noise, so the isotropic theory does not apply, and a coloured-noise generalisation is named as needed. Then Property 1 still declares the edge "detected" as a departure from that same isotropic prediction, and the MP edge is drawn on the spectrum plot. This folder has met the same structural error from the other direction (run 706: an inflated norm will usually reproduce an effect you attributed to structure), but this is the cleanest statement of it at the level of a *null* rather than a control. Mechanical rule for us: **an empirical detection claim is stated against a noise band measured from the same data (shuffled windows, held-out seeds, permuted time order), not against a theoretical null the same paper has shown to be wrong by orders of magnitude - because a structured-noise distribution has fat tails, and a ratio threshold calibrated on the isotropic prediction sits inside the noise.** Cross-reference run 706 (variance is not magnitude, norm-matched control), run 708 (a scale at initialisation decides what the fit finds later), run 713 (survey-sourced numbers are inherited, never re-measured - here the null is inherited and never re-measured either).

That interpretation is almost certainly right, and it is also the reason the companion grokking claim needs scrutiny: a window of W deltas at 200-step checkpoint spacing spans 200W steps, so at W = 10 the horizon is 2,000 steps, and the 1,700-step grokking lead reported from companion work is *shorter than the integration horizon of the statistic that produced it*. A slow moving average leading a fast series by roughly its own averaging length is a mathematical certainty, not evidence of a precursor. Mechanical rule for us: **every monitoring statistic we propose that is a rolling-window functional states its integration horizon in the same sentence as its lead time, and if the lead is comparable to or shorter than that horizon the result is reported as a level threshold rather than as a precursor - because the only thing that distinguishes a genuine early warning from an artefact of smoothing is a lead time that survives shortening the window.** Cross-reference run 712 (a between-checkpoint gap is not a transition; two transitions separated 10-20x in tokens), run 708 (a stability claim is worth more as a curve over a sweep than as a point).

- **Pattern:** **A trajectory feature must be an integral, not a peak and not a spread - and this entry is the sharpest demonstration in the folder of why, because the artifact it defeats is one the folder has been treating as a finding.** Pythia's layer-0 heads begin at a participation ratio near 60 (random attention spreads mass across all positions, so the effective rank is high at initialisation) and collapse to 2-30 by the end of training, so ranking heads by spread - max minus min - puts exactly those collapsing heads at the top; ranking by the time integral of the clipped positive part demotes them and surfaces heads that *gain* sustained rank. The head-to-head table makes the size of the error visible: precision-at-30 is 0.93 for spread against 0.97 for the integral, but mean selectivity in the top five is 155x against 5,791x. Note what this does to every entry in this folder that read a dominant direction or a high rank out of a final checkpoint: a high effective rank is the *default* state of a random head, so the interesting quantity is not how high the rank is but how long it stayed high relative to where it started. Mechanical rule for us: **every trajectory-derived feature we define is specified as a functional of the whole curve - monotone in sustained behaviour, clipped or baseline-subtracted against its value at initialisation, and normalised by fraction of training rather than raw step count - and we print the spread-based and peak-based alternatives beside it, because on this panel the naive alternatives rank the random-init collapse as the top result while the integral ranks the actual specialists.** Cross-reference run 712 (a percentile threshold is stable while the maximum swings two orders of magnitude - the same lesson, one statistic upstream), run 708 (a scale at initialisation decides what the fit finds later).
- **Pattern:** **A circuit can be causally necessary in one seed and causally irrelevant in another trained on identical data with identical hyperparameters - the six-seed cross-ablation matrix is the cleanest negative in the folder and it constrains every "the circuit for X" claim we will ever make.** s42 implements the retrieval task with four layer-0 heads; s271 uses L6H{1,10} plus L7H{9,15} with no layer-0 head above a spread of 11. - **Done:** arxiv-2604.10098 - Attention Sink in Transformers: A Survey on Utilization, Interpretation, and Mitigation (read full text v2: abstract, §1-§9 including the conclusion and the §9 limitations paragraph, with §2.1-§2.6 architecture-by-architecture, §3.1-§3.4, §4.1-§4.5 and the five-level synthesis table, §5.1-§5.5, §6.1-§6.9 and §7.1-§7.2 read in full; Appendix A Table 1, the per-paper summary of surveyed work, located but not read row by row; Figures 1-42 read from captions and the prose that reports them, not inspected as images; reference list read only as far as resolving works named in the text)
- **Pattern:** **The survey's one structural claim worth carrying is that its eleven accounts are arranged by the *kind* of thing each explains, not by which is right - and that arrangement is the audit this folder has been missing.** The five levels are mathematical origin (softmax no-op; structural bias from causal masking and RoPE), training dynamics (active-dormant head reinforcement - the only account placed on that level), numerical mechanism (outlier circuits; outlier-driven rescaling; mix-compress-refine), geometric structure (geometric anchoring; anti-overmixing; spectral-energy association), and functional role (implicit attention bias). Placed against entries 704-712, this folder holds an independent reading of nearly every one of them, which converts the survey from a source of new mechanism into a **coverage and redundancy check**: the levels with only one account each in the whole literature are training dynamics and functional role, and those are exactly the levels where our own predictive ambitions sit. Mechanical rule for us: **whenever we add an account of a mechanism, we record which level it operates on and which other accounts occupy that level, and an account that is the sole occupant of its level is treated as untested rather than as established - because "no competitor" in this literature means "no one has built one", not "it survived".** Cross-reference run 704 (path-product bound: a mathematical-origin-level account), run 706 (link-by-link weight trace: numerical-mechanism level), run 710/711 (training-dynamics level, where every entry had to import its own dynamics experiment).
- **Pattern:** **Survey evidence is second-hand, and this document shows how second-hand it is at the level of the single number that the whole no-op account rests on.** The two classified evidence it marshals for the no-op family are observational (sink tokens have small value states, across BERT, ViT, LLaMA, OLMo and KV-quantization work) and causal (relax the sum-to-one constraint and the sink goes away - gating, clipped softmax, a `+1` denominator, an unnormalized rectified softmax, plain sigmoid), and every magnitude it quotes is inherited from the cited paper rather than re-measured; the survey's own study count is given as "over 210", "over 200" and "over 180" in three different sections. Note what this does to the *causal* half specifically: it is exactly the move runs 705-711 showed can be a relocation rather than a removal. Mechanical rule for us: **no survey-sourced number enters our own writing as a measurement - it enters as a pointer to the primary paper, and any account we adopt on survey authority alone is marked unverified until we have read the cited primary source; and where a survey's own internal counts disagree, that disagreement is recorded rather than averaged.** Cross-reference run 708 (a stability claim worth more as a curve than as a point), run 711 (mitigation success scored as a relocation), run 706 (the norm-matched control that made a correlation into a mechanism).
- **Pattern:** **Whether a sink "matters" is an architecture-level fact, not a sink-level one - and the survey's ablation table is the folder's widest cross-architecture sample of that.** ViTs degrade severely when their sink tokens are ablated; diffusion transformers lose almost nothing in text alignment but shift fine-grained perceptual structure by roughly six times a random-masking control; diffusion language models barely degrade at all because their sinks move during generation instead of sitting at a fixed position; MoE LLMs collapse entirely when three of several thousand experts are pruned; and in DiTs the sink carries semantic scene information rather than nullity, so the null-token reading of the word does not survive contact with that family. Read together with runs 704-712 this means the folder's most portable finding is a *conditional*: a sink is load-bearing to the degree the model's computation has been routed through the address. Mechanical rule for us: **every claim that a component is causally necessary is reported with the architecture family it was measured in and the ablation's damage on the sub-task the mechanism is supposed to serve, and a single-family ablation is never generalized into a statement about sinks as such - because the same ablation that zeroes a benchmark in one family leaves another family's quality unchanged, and the difference is the architecture's answer to "what else could carry this".** Cross-reference run 704 (deleting the first token zeroes RULER at 4096 context in Gemma 7B while costing nothing in a model trained without a fixed beginning token), run 711 (gating deletes NOP sinks and multiplies broadcast sinks fortyfold - the same family-internal version of the same lesson).

Developmental Trajectories of Capability and Attention-Sink Emergence Across Three 1B-Class Architectures (read full text v2: abstract, §1-§13 including related work and the full limitations section, all six findings with Tables 1-8, §8.1 null-calibration table, §11.1-§11.4 discussion including the exploratory activation-versus-weight spectral bridge and its Spearman values; Figures 1-3 read from captions and the prose that reports them, not inspected as images; reference list read only as far as resolving the works cited in §§1-2 and §11.3)
- **Pattern:** **A negative result about where a mechanism can live is cheaper and sharper than a positive result about what it is - the L0/L1 zero-BOS floor is now a falsification test for any account in this cluster.** Zero heads classify as first-token in layers 0 and 1 at every one of the 30 sampled revisions across two corpora and two architecture families, from random initialisation to trillions of tokens, so the phenomenon every entry from 704 onward described at a final checkpoint is bounded by an identity that holds throughout training. Note what this does to the folder: a mechanistic theory that predicts sinks from residual-stream statistics must also predict that the two shallowest layers are off-limits, and the author's own qualitative reading - that position 0's embedding is a fixed function of one token, so attending there discards content until depth has mixed positions - is exactly the kind of claim our white-box model should be forced to make explicitly. Mechanical rule for us: **for every mechanism we claim, we also state where in the stack it must NOT appear and verify that at every checkpoint we have, because a prediction that a component can be anywhere is unfalsifiable, and a floor that holds across 30 runs and two corpora is one of the few identity-like statements this literature has produced.** Cross-reference run 704 (removing the first token breaks the model in exactly the sub-task the mechanism serves), run 710 (the sink's position is chosen by the data pipeline, not the architecture - here the layer position is chosen by the architecture and cannot be moved by the pipeline).
- **Pattern:** **Circuit membership is not the circuit - the same capability is implemented by a different set of heads as training proceeds, and what happens to a decayed head decides whether it was retired or moved.** Formation-time and final induction circuits share only about a third of their heads (Jaccard 0.29-0.33, stable across screen thresholds), and the same group ablation gives opposite readings depending on fate: heads that decayed into sinks go inert (Pythia, +0.3 points, z = +1.0) while heads that slid into the duplicate-token role stay causal (OLMoE L6·H1, -3.1 points, z = -5.5), and a head that was never an induction head at all but only a duplicate detector is causally necessary for induction (L3·H15, -3.2 against -0.48 for matched-random controls). The cleanest part is the within-model comparison: OLMoE's own sink-fate decayer is inert and its own duplicate-fate decayers are causal, so the "dense turns over, MoE accretes" contrast is an aggregate artefact of which fate the heads happened to take. Mechanical rule for us: **any circuit or feature set we identify at one point in a process is reported with its overlap against the same identification at another point, plus a fate for every element that dropped out - because a screening criterion measures the pattern it screens for, and a unit that stops showing that pattern may have moved inside the circuit rather than left it; the second case is invisible to the screen and shows up only as an ablation that still bites.** Cross-reference run 704 (a no-op write is a learned else-branch, not an inactive unit), run 711 (a signature vanishing without showing where the computation went is a relocation, not a fix).
- **Pattern:** **Two quantities that look like one statistic are not interchangeable, and the developmental panel is what separates them - a percentile threshold is stable across training while a maximum swings by two orders of magnitude.** Null-selectivity p99 holds in a 1.45-2.08x band across 140K steps, so a threshold calibrated once at the final checkpoint applies throughout; null-selectivity max wanders from 7.3 to 767 over the same revisions because it is set by isolated pathological draws (a concentrated head whose preferred target happens to align with a random null position). The same lesson appears in the headline result from the other side: the induction transition and the sink transition look like one event at a single checkpoint and separate by 10-20x in tokens once both are tracked across revisions (11.5x on OLMo, 21x on OLMoE), and the same DCLM corpus produces a sharp jump under dense OLMo and a gradual ramp under MoE OLMoE. Mechanical rule for us: **whenever our read-out depends on a threshold or a summary of a distribution, we state which functional of that distribution it is and check its stability across the checkpoints or seeds we have, and we never compare a curve's shape between two models unless the sampling grid is identical - because a maximum is not a threshold, a between-checkpoint gap is not a transition, and a one-checkpoint comparison cannot tell one transition from two.** Cross-reference run 710 (a scalar regulariser swings a sink statistic threefold), run 705 (the same gate reads as flat or selective depending on which normalisation the statistic lives in).

- **Pattern:** **The same observable is compatible with two opposite computations, and the cheap discriminator is not the observable but the norm and the rank of what the attended position writes - this is the entry that finally gives the folder a scale on which its own sink statistics are ambiguous.** Every entry from 704 onward measured concentration, and concentration separates nothing: a NOP sink (near-zero value) and a broadcast sink (content-scale value, rank-one update) both produce a stripe, are both present in the same pretrained DINOv2-G, and both pass any sink-fraction count. The two modes are so distinguishable that a two-number projection of the same model splits them cleanly, but only once the value norm ratio and the update rank are added to the attention matrix. Mechanical rule for us: **no attention-concentration statistic is reported alone - it ships as a triple (fraction of attention mass on the destination, norm of what that destination writes relative to the head's ordinary values, rank of the resulting update), because a near-zero write and a rank-one shared write are identical in every pure-attention view we have been taking, and the write is what the residual stream actually receives.** Cross-reference run 705 (the same gate reading as flat or selective depending on which normalisation the statistic lives in), run 710 (the sink-fraction statistic swung threefold by weight decay alone - a statistic with no mechanism attached).
- **Pattern:** **Interventions must be split by what they leave intact, and this paper is the cleanest statement in the folder of the difference between touching the payload and touching the routing.** Value patching holds the learned attention matrix fixed, so it asks what information sits at the destination; removing the sink column and renormalising asks whether routing through the destination was necessary at all, and everything downstream is destroyed with it - the authors label the second a necessity test and refuse to read it as selective removal. The payoff is a case where the two disagree: in the controlled broadcast model the layer-one sink is causally necessary by every routing and zero-ablation measure, yet donor patching there transfers almost nothing (payload alignment 0.162 against 0.944 at layer two), so "this sink matters" and "this sink is the channel" come apart in the same model. Mechanical rule for us: **when we patch or ablate a component we state which of the three things the intervention preserves - the direction of the write, the routing to it, or neither - and we do not infer that a component carries a signal from the fact that deleting it hurts, because a necessary relay that carries nothing transferable fails exactly that way.** Cross-reference run 707 (a radial map designed so the forward and backward effects separate by construction), run 705 (a bound tested with the upstream gradients held fixed).
- **Pattern:** **An intervention that removes a mechanism does not remove the computation - the model routes it somewhere else, and the somewhere else is measurable.** Gating deletes detected NOP sinks outright (0.25 to 0.00 per image) and broadcast sinks multiply from 0.09 to 3.80, forty times over; registers absorb most sink mass and then divide into the same two phenotypes; the penalised global pathway was designed as a place for the shared computation to live and it takes the causal load off attention entirely in the controlled task (removing the attention update leaves task MSE at 0.3648, removing the global pathway raises it to 1.6539). And the variant that suppresses broadcast most effectively is the one that performs worst on dense probes, so the mitigation leaderboard and the representation-quality leaderboard are anti-correlated. Mechanical rule for us: **every architectural or training intervention we propose is scored on the full set of behaviours it could have displaced, plus downstream quality, and an experiment that shows a signature vanishing without showing where the computation went is reported as a relocation, not a fix - because an intervention that removes a sink can convert one null write into forty shared writes, and the score we designed the intervention to improve will not see that.** Cross-reference run 704 (removing the first token breaks the model in exactly the sub-task the mechanism serves), run 709 (a gate that survives its own routing being deleted is the gate that was the mechanism).

- **Pattern:** **The paper manufactures the mechanism as an explicit parameter and then varies its magnitude continuously - the bias ladder is the cheapest causal instrument in this cluster and the value-bias sweep is its best result.** Key bias alone (value bias fixed at zero) relocates the sink off the first token while validation loss stays at 3.72, so the key-side score is doing the work and the value-side write is decoration. The sweep then shows the reverse direction: raise the length of the fixed value bias and attention migrates *back* from the bias to the first token (sink on the bias 73.34 -> 1.51 at twenty times the unit vector's length, with the first-token sink rising to 25.88), because a large value write is expensive to cancel inside the residual stream, so the optimiser re-points the keys of token one to absorb the same surplus. Mechanical rule for us: **when we claim a component supplies a function, we instantiate that function as an explicit parameter at the same position, hold the rest of the architecture fixed, and sweep the parameter through at least three magnitudes - because a knob that switches a behaviour on, off, and back off again at the far end is a claim about the fitted solution rather than about the component, and the far end is where the reason shows itself.** Cross-reference run 705 (a mechanism versus a scale knob separated by replacing selection with its average), run 708 (a derived parameter reported beside the swept optimum).

- **Pattern:** **A component published inside a bundle may not be the part doing the work, and this paper's Appendix A.1 is the cleanest self-inflicted demonstration in the head.** The prior work this paper positions against was named for routing — a sigmoid that selects the top-k among pools of key/value/output experts — and when the authors collapse the selection to a single expert, deleting the routing mechanism entirely and leaving only the sigmoid on the value output, that single-expert configuration is the best row in the whole switch-head family on both perplexity (5.808) and benchmarks, while the largest routing configuration (8 experts, top-8) is worse and costs 38M parameters against 3M. Note the shape of the move: instead of arguing that routing matters less than reported, they remove it and re-measure the same family, which converts a bundled claim into a single-component claim at the cost of one training run per row. Mechanical rule for us: **when we attribute an effect to a selection, routing or competition mechanism, we rerun the comparison with the selection collapsed to a single option — same gate, same slots, no choice — and report that row beside the full mechanism, because a gate that survives its own routing being deleted is the gate that was the mechanism, and everything we would have said about "specialisation" belongs to the routing we just removed.** Cross-reference run 705 (a mechanism and a scale knob are indistinguishable unless the selective part is replaced by its own average - the same collapse of a selector, from the other side), run 704 (a unit whose write is near-zero is the load-bearing unit; here a module whose selection never selects is).
- **Pattern:** **Two named factors in one architectural addition can be separated by substituting, at the same position, a cheaper component that supplies only one of them - and that is what the RMSNorm row and the non-sparse-sigmoid row do here.** The gate was credited with two things: a non-linearity in a path that the algebra shows collapses into one low-rank map (value projection composed with output projection, further narrowed by grouped-query attention), and an input-dependent sparse score. A parameter-free RMSNorm at the identical position supplies only the non-linearity and still cuts average perplexity from 6.026 to 5.847, while a rescaled sigmoid confined to [0.5, 1.0] supplies only the non-linearity-and-gate-shape without the small scores and gives 5.900; but only the genuinely sparse, query-dependent gate drops the first-token attention share from 0.467 to 0.048, while the non-sparse gate leaves it at 0.451. So the perplexity gain and the sink suppression are carried by different halves, and neither half alone reproduces the other's effect. Mechanical rule for us: **when we credit a component with more than one job, we name each job and exhibit one substitute that supplies that job alone — in the head we already do this for "does this direction do anything" and "is this a scale artefact", but not yet for multi-purpose components — because a single ablation that removes the component removes all its jobs at once, and reports the sum as though it were the mechanism.** Cross-reference run 706 (variance versus magnitude separated by a norm-matched control), run 707 (magnitude and direction separated by three ratios before any conclusion), run 700 (a gain needs a null that spends the same budget - here the rival null is a parameter-free normaliser).

- **Pattern:** **A removed normaliser's functional role can be *restored analytically* by solving for one parameter, and this entry is the head's cleanest case of a hyperparameter that was derived rather than tuned.** Softmax supplied two things the elementwise sigmoid does not: per-element mass of about 1/n, and a specific gradient scale with respect to a logit. Requiring the sigmoid gates to sum to one yields a single solving bias bounded between −log(n−1)−M and −log(n−1)−m (Proposition E.1), and requiring the gate's derivative to match softmax's yields the same order −log n; the empirical sweep over constant biases then peaks near −10 and degrades at −15, which is the same order for the sequence lengths used. Mechanical rule for us: **whenever our white-box model replaces or drops a component of the network, we state the property that component supplied, solve for the parameter that restores it, and report the solved value beside the empirically best one - because a replacement whose only tuning is a sweep has not shown what the original component was for, and a derived value that lands near the sweep's optimum is evidence the explanation of the component is right.** Cross-reference run 707 (the intermediate quantity that transmits a training signal, named rather than correlated), run 704 (a bound that predicts the direction of an effect before it is measured).
- **Pattern:** **A stability claim is cheaper and more informative when it is a *curve over a sweep* rather than a point at one setting - and the LR-sensitivity score here is the reusable form of that.** The score is the expected excess loss over a learning-rate grid relative to the best learning rate on that grid, so a flat score means the configuration tolerates a wrong learning rate; the paper reads every ablation through it (LayerScale on/off, QK norm on/off) and treats "no spikes in gradient norm" with smooth loss as a success criterion in its own right. The same discipline appears in the bias ablation as a non-monotone curve with an interior optimum, which no single-setting comparison could have revealed. Mechanical rule for us: **any intervention or architectural variant we evaluate is reported as a curve over its own strength or over the learning rate, with the summary statistic stated (here an expected excess over the best point), and a single-setting success is not counted as a robustness result - because the interesting failure in this paper is at the *ends* of the range, and a sweep midpoint would have looked like a clean win.** Cross-reference run 703 (the plateau-then-cliff curve, where a correlation was being read off the flat part), run 700 (a gain needs a null that spends the same budget).
- **Pattern:** **The failure that cost prior work its result was a *scale at step zero*, invisible in final accuracy - and this paper's whole contribution is finding it by looking at an initialisation statistic.** Naive sigmoid attention was reported to work, did not reproduce, and the diagnosis was the initial attention output norm being large, fixed by moving initial logit mass into the sigmoid's near-zero region (ALiBi, or the −log n bias). Note what the fix has in common across the two routes: both reduce a norm at initialisation while leaving the trained function class alone, and the paper's own FLOP accounting shows the arithmetic difference between the two activations is negligible, so the entire gap was never about the activation's cost or capacity. Mechanical rule for us: **when a mechanism or a read-out "does not transfer" between two models, the first diagnostic is a scale statistic measured at initialisation or at the start of the fit, printed for both models - because a difference in initial geometry produces a difference in what the fit later finds, and an end-state comparison will attribute that difference to the mechanism under study.** Cross-reference run 707 (a normalisation that makes magnitude and direction inseparable, separated by ratios), run 706 (variance versus magnitude separated by a norm-matched control), run 701/702 (the offset ratio, the same statistic one level up: what the layer is fed decides what it learns).
